words.enDefinition: the extra usable output that occurs when actual process loss is lower than normal expected loss

examples.en: The exercise reported an abnormal gain because the batch lost fewer units than the expected amount.
examples.zh: 那一批损耗件数低于预期，练习报告了「异常增益」。

examples.en: We calculated the abnormal gain in units before explaining how it changed the department's cost report.
examples.zh: 我们先按单位数计算「异常增益」，再解释它如何改变部门成本报告。

words.enDefinition: spoilage beyond what is normally expected under efficient production conditions

examples.en: The broken printer caused abnormal spoilage because far more covers were unusable than we usually expected.
examples.zh: 打印机故障使无法使用的封面远多于通常预计，造成了「异常废品损失」。

examples.en: The costs of abnormal spoilage were shown separately in the exercise rather than charged to ordinary output.
examples.zh: 练习把「异常废品损失」单列，没有计入正常产出。

collocations: record a loss from abnormal spoilage

words.enDefinition: a difference stated in the original units between two values

examples.en: The worksheet listed absolute change in pounds before calculating the percentage movement in sales.
examples.zh: 练习表先用英镑列出「变动额」，再算销售额变动的百分比。

examples.en: We compared the absolute change in expenses for both stores before discussing their different sizes.
examples.zh: 我们先比较了两家商店费用的「变动额」，然后讨论规模差异。

collocations: the absolute change in operating costs

words.enDefinition: an income statement using inventory and cost of goods sold that include allocated fixed manufacturing overhead

examples.en: The absorption costing income statement included allocated fixed manufacturing costs in the cost of units sold.
examples.zh: 「完全成本法利润表」把已分配的固定制造费用计入已售单位的成本。

examples.en: We compared the absorption costing income statement with the version that showed contribution margin separately.
examples.zh: 我们把「完全成本法利润表」和单独列出边际贡献的那张表作了比较。

collocations: prepare an absorption costing income statement
review an absorption costing income statement
figures in an absorption costing income statement

words.enDefinition: room to exercise judgement within permitted accounting choices

examples.en: The tutor discussed accounting discretion when two fictional businesses made different assumptions about useful lives.
examples.zh: 两家虚构企业对使用寿命作出不同假设时，导师讨论了「会计判断裁量权」。

examples.en: We asked how accounting discretion affected comparability between the sample company and its industry peers.
examples.zh: 我们问，「会计判断裁量权」会如何影响样本公司与同行的可比性。

collocations: compare the use of accounting discretion

words.enDefinition: Data and assumptions used in a measurement method to develop an estimated financial amount.

examples.en: The class checked accounting estimate inputs before deciding whether the expected repair costs had genuinely changed.
examples.zh: 大家先核查了「会计估计输入值」，再判断预计维修成本是否真的变了。

examples.en: The note showed that new customer data changed accounting estimate inputs while the measurement technique stayed the same.
examples.zh: 附注说明，新的客户数据改变了「会计估计输入值」，计量技术没有变化。

collocations: explain changes in accounting estimate inputs

words.enDefinition: Choosing the accounting principles or methods used for a transaction under the applicable reporting framework.

examples.en: The case focused on accounting policy selection for a transaction that no standard addressed directly.
examples.zh: 例题重点讨论在没有准则直接适用时，如何对一项交易作「会计政策选择」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how accounting policy selection could affect comparability between companies that hold similar assets.
examples.zh: 老师问，「会计政策选择」会怎样影响持有相似资产的公司之间的可比性。

collocations: review the basis for accounting policy selection

words.enDefinition: the portion of earnings attributable to accruals rather than cash flow

examples.en: The worksheet estimated the accrual component of profit using the two reported figures provided.
examples.zh: 练习表根据提供的两个报告数字估算盈利的「应计部分」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the accrual component might reverse in the next period in the example.
examples.zh: 导师问，示例中的「应计部分」是否可能在下一期转回。

collocations: compare the accrual component across periods

words.enDefinition: how closely accruals reflect or predict associated cash flows

examples.en: The tutor compared accrual quality for businesses with very different patterns of cash collection.
examples.zh: 导师比较了收款规律差异很大的企业的「应计项目质量」。

examples.en: We examined accrual quality after the sample's estimated collections moved further from actual cash receipts.
examples.zh: 样本估计收款与实际现金到账额的差距扩大后，我们研究了其「应计项目质量」。

words.enDefinition: accruals scaled by a stated measure such as average assets

examples.en: The accrual ratio in the exercise expressed total accruals as a share of average assets.
examples.zh: 练习中的「应计比率」用应计项目总额占平均资产的比例表示。

examples.en: We checked the formula in the footnote before comparing the accrual ratio across two fictional businesses.
examples.zh: 我们先核对脚注中的公式，再比较两家虚构企业的「应计比率」。

collocations: the denominator of an accrual ratio

words.zhGloss: 收购业务支付的现金净额
words.enDefinition: cash paid for an acquired business less the cash and cash equivalents included in the acquired business
acceptedZhAnswers: 收购业务支付的现金净额

examples.en: The investing section reported the acquisition net of cash acquired after the buyer obtained control of the company.
examples.zh: 买方取得公司控制权后，投资部分列出了「收购业务支付的现金净额」。

examples.en: The class calculated the acquisition net of cash acquired using cash consideration and the subsidiary's cash balance.
examples.zh: 课堂用现金购买对价和子公司的现金余额计算了「收购业务支付的现金净额」。

collocations: report an acquisition net of cash acquired
calculate the acquisition net of cash acquired
present an acquisition net of cash acquired

words.enDefinition: obtaining control of an entity so that it becomes a subsidiary of the acquiring entity

examples.en: The group's acquisition of a subsidiary was reported separately from the purchase of individual machines during the year.
examples.zh: 集团的「取得子公司」与年内购置单台机器的事项分开列报。

examples.en: We read the note on the acquisition of a subsidiary to identify how much cash the buyer paid.
examples.zh: 我们阅读了有关「取得子公司」的附注，以确定买方支付了多少现金。

collocations: disclose the acquisition of a subsidiary
finance the acquisition of a subsidiary
account for the acquisition of a subsidiary

words.enDefinition: expenses incurred in connection with acquiring another business

examples.en: The sample listed acquisition-related costs for advisers and due diligence in its adjustment table.
examples.zh: 样本在调整表中列出了顾问和尽职调查产生的「收购相关费用」。

examples.en: Our group checked which acquisition-related costs the fictional company had excluded from its adjusted figure.
examples.zh: 小组核对了虚构公司在调整后指标中剔除了哪些「收购相关费用」。

words.zhGloss: 通过租赁取得资产使用权
words.enDefinition: obtaining the right to use an asset under a lease agreement
acceptedZhAnswers: 通过租赁取得资产使用权

examples.en: An acquisition through a lease gave the company use of new equipment without an upfront cash payment.
examples.zh: 公司「通过租赁取得资产使用权」，无需预付现金就能使用新设备。

examples.en: The note separated acquisition through a lease from outright equipment purchases that required cash at the outset.
examples.zh: 附注将「通过租赁取得资产使用权」与一开始就要付现的设备直接购置分开说明。

collocations: account for acquisition through a lease
compare acquisition through a lease with purchase

words.enDefinition: A method that estimates the activities needed to meet planned demand and budgets for their resources.

examples.en: We used activity-based budgeting to estimate how much time the returns desk would spend checking each batch.
examples.zh: 我们通过「作业基础预算编制」，估算退货服务台检查每批货要花多少时间。

examples.en: The worksheet used activity-based budgeting to turn expected repair orders into planned inspection and testing hours.
examples.zh: 练习表用「作业基础预算编制」把预计维修订单换算成计划检查和测试工时。

words.enDefinition: a costing method assigning resource costs to activities and then to objects based on their use of those activities

examples.en: Our shop applied activity-based costing after discovering that small orders required most of the setup work.
examples.zh: 发现小单占用了大部分准备工作后，店里采用了「作业成本法」。

examples.en: The lecturer used activity-based costing to compare products requiring different numbers of inspections before sale.
examples.zh: 讲师用「作业成本法」比较售前检查次数不同的几种产品。

words.enDefinition: using information about activities and their costs to manage resources and improve operations

examples.en: We used activity-based management to identify repeat inspections that added little value for customers.
examples.zh: 我们用「基于作业的管理」找出对顾客价值不大的重复检查。

examples.en: The class linked activity-based management to changes the workshop could make in its order process.
examples.zh: 课堂把「基于作业的管理」和工作室在订单流程中可作的调整联系了起来。

words.enDefinition: a grouping of costs associated with a particular activity for subsequent allocation

examples.en: We placed checking and packing costs in separate groups, starting with the inspection activity cost pool.
examples.zh: 我们把检查和打包费用分组，先归集与检验有关的「作业成本库」。

examples.en: The activity cost pool contained expenses connected with preparing the printer for each different batch.
examples.zh: 该「作业成本库」归集了给打印机更换批次、做好准备的相关费用。

collocations: group costs in an activity cost pool
assign costs to an activity cost pool
select a driver for an activity cost pool

words.enDefinition: a description of the different activities used in a costing system and how they are defined

examples.en: We recorded each stage of packing in the activity dictionary so both departments used the same terms.
examples.zh: 我们在「作业字典」记录打包各环节，让两个部门都用同一套词。

examples.en: The activity dictionary explained what counted as an inspection in the print shop's costing model.
examples.zh: 「作业字典」解释了在印刷店的成本模型里，哪些工作算一次检查。

collocations: define activities in an activity dictionary

words.enDefinition: a measure of how much of an activity a product, service or other cost object consumes

examples.en: We chose the number of setups as the activity driver for the workshop's preparation costs.
examples.zh: 我们用设备准备次数作为工作室准备成本的「作业动因」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether the activity driver reflected actual inspection effort for all the products.
examples.zh: 讲师问，「作业动因」能不能反映所有产品实际需要的检查工作量。

words.enDefinition: the cost assigned per unit of the driver used to measure an activity

examples.en: We calculated the activity rate for inspections using estimated inspection costs and the expected inspection count.
examples.zh: 我们用估算的检查成本和预计检查次数计算了检查的「作业成本分配率」。

examples.en: The worksheet applied the activity rate to the number of setups each product needed that week.
examples.zh: 练习表把「作业成本分配率」乘以当周每种产品所需的准备次数。

words.enDefinition: The difference between the flexible and original budgets caused by a change in activity level.

examples.en: The activity variance showed what changed when we used the actual number of workshops in the budget.
examples.zh: 「业务量差异」说明了，预算改用实际工作坊场次后会有什么变化。

examples.en: Our tutor calculated the activity variance before comparing actual spending with the budget at actual activity.
examples.zh: 老师先算了「业务量差异」，再把实际支出和按实际业务量编制的预算比较。

collocations: separate the activity variance from spending effects

words.enDefinition: An internal charge based on the costs actually incurred by production

examples.en: The actual-cost transfer price rose when the supplying unit paid more for materials.
examples.zh: 供应分部多付了材料费之后，「实际成本内部转移价」提高了。

examples.en: Our comparison showed how a delay affected the actual-cost transfer price that month.
examples.zh: 我们的比较显示，延期怎样影响当期的「实际成本内部转移价」。

collocations: compare an actual-cost transfer price with a standard

words.enDefinition: a method using actual direct costs and overhead assigned with an actual rate based on actual costs and activity

examples.en: The exercise used actual costing after we had final figures for materials, labour and indirect expenses.
examples.zh: 我们拿到材料、人工和间接费用的最终数字后，练习采用了「实际成本法」。

examples.en: We compared actual costing with a method that assigned overhead using the estimated annual rate.
examples.zh: 我们把「实际成本法」和一种采用预估年度费率分配间接费用的做法作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the number of hours paid for under a labour cost calculation, including paid idle hours if present

examples.en: The actual hours paid included twenty minutes when the class technicians were waiting for replacement parts.
examples.zh: 「实际付薪工时」包含课堂案例里的技工等待替换零件的二十分钟。

examples.en: The wage record showed the actual hours paid, while a separate sheet recorded time spent assembling units.
examples.zh: 工资记录显示「实际付薪工时」，另一张表则记着花在组装产品上的时间。

collocations: compare actual hours paid with hours worked
use actual hours paid to calculate the hourly rate

words.enDefinition: The labour cost actually incurred per hour for the hours and workers being compared.

examples.en: The actual labour rate went up when the workshop assigned a more experienced technician to the repairs.
examples.zh: 工场派更有经验的技工来维修后，「实际人工费率」提高了。

examples.en: We divided wage cost by paid hours to find the actual labour rate for the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 我们用工资成本除以付薪工时，得出了课堂练习里的「实际人工费率」。

collocations: an actual labour rate above standard
multiply the actual labour rate by actual hours

words.enDefinition: The proportions in which different materials were actually used in a process.

examples.en: The actual material mix contained more recycled fibre than the blend given on the standard cost worksheet.
examples.zh: 「实际材料配比」里的再生纤维比例高于标准成本练习表上的配比。

examples.en: We reconstructed the actual material mix from the weights written down for each trial batch.
examples.zh: 我们用记录下来的各试验批次材料重量，还原了「实际材料配比」。

collocations: compare the actual material mix with the recipe
a change in the actual material mix

words.enDefinition: The cost per unit actually paid or charged for the material in the calculation.

examples.en: The case included freight in the actual material price because it was part of acquiring the fabric.
examples.zh: 案例把运费计入「实际材料单价」，因为那是购入布料的一部分成本。

examples.en: After the second invoice arrived, the class calculated the actual material price per sheet of card stock.
examples.zh: 第二张发票到后，同学们计算了每张卡纸的「实际材料单价」。

collocations: compare the actual material price with the standard
the actual material price per kilogram

words.enDefinition: The amount of material consumed during the production or activity being measured.

examples.en: Our worksheet compared the actual material quantity used with the allowance for the same number of signs.
examples.zh: 练习表把「实际材料用量」与同等数量标牌对应的标准用量作比较。

examples.en: We weighed the leftover dough to check the actual material quantity used in the morning batch.
examples.zh: 我们称了剩余面团，以核对早晨这批产品的「实际材料用量」。

collocations: record the actual material quantity used
measure the actual material quantity used
compare the actual material quantity used with the standard

words.enDefinition: The usable output actually obtained per unit of input during a run or period.

examples.en: The actual output yield fell when several of the sample tiles cracked before they could be packed.
examples.zh: 几块样品瓷砖还没打包就裂了，「实际产出率」随之下降。

examples.en: We measured the actual output yield in finished labels per metre of paper fed into the printer.
examples.zh: 我们的「实际产出率」以每送进打印机一米纸印出多少张成品标签来衡量。

collocations: record a below-standard actual output yield
compare the actual output yield across batches

words.enDefinition: the indirect costs that were incurred during a period, before comparing them with allocated amounts

examples.en: The accountant added rent and equipment repairs to find actual overhead for the small workshop.
examples.zh: 会计把租金和设备维修费相加，求得这间小工作室「实际发生的间接费用」。

examples.en: In the exercise, actual overhead was higher because two machines needed unexpected maintenance that month.
examples.zh: 练习中，两台机器当月需要临时维护，「实际发生的间接费用」因此更高。

collocations: compare actual overhead with applied overhead

words.enDefinition: The number of units of an input bought during the period, whether already used or still on hand.

examples.en: The actual quantity purchased was higher than production use because the workshop kept some fabric for next month.
examples.zh: 「实际采购量」高于生产用量，因为工场留了一些布料到下个月用。

examples.en: Use the actual quantity purchased for this price calculation, including the wood still in the storeroom.
examples.zh: 这道价格计算题用「实际采购量」，也就是把仍在库房的木材算进去。

collocations: the actual quantity purchased during the month
multiply the actual quantity purchased by the price difference

words.enDefinition: The proportions of individual products in the total number of units actually sold.

examples.en: The actual sales mix shifted towards the smaller mugs even though the stall sold the same total number.
examples.zh: 摊位卖出的杯子总数相同，但「实际销售组合」向小杯倾斜了。

examples.en: We used the receipt counts for each design to find the actual sales mix in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习里，我们用收据上各款式的销量找出「实际销售组合」。

collocations: a shift in the actual sales mix
compare the actual sales mix with the budget

words.enDefinition: an amount added back to a measure in an adjustment

examples.en: The classroom reconciliation included an add-back for an expense excluded from the adjusted profit measure.
examples.zh: 课堂调节表把从调整后利润指标中剔除的一项费用作为「加回项」。

examples.en: We checked which original charge the add-back in the table was meant to reverse.
examples.zh: 我们核对了表里的「加回项」是为了抵销哪笔原始费用。

collocations: an expense listed as an add-back

words.expression: add back a loss on disposal
words.lemma: add back a loss on disposal
words.enDefinition: to restore a disposal loss deducted in starting profit when reconciling profit to operating cash flow
acceptedEnVariants: add back a loss on disposal

examples.en: We needed to add back a loss on disposal before reporting the sale proceeds under investing cash flows.
examples.zh: 在投资现金流项下列报出售所得之前，我们需要「加回处置损失」。

examples.en: The exercise asked where to add back a loss on disposal that had reduced the starting profit amount.
examples.zh: 练习问，应该在哪里「加回处置损失」，这笔损失已经扣减了起始利润金额。

collocations: add back a loss on disposal to profit
add back a loss on disposal in the reconciliation
remember to add back a loss on disposal

words.enDefinition: Expense arising solely because extra work requires another staff shift

examples.en: The forecast added an additional shift cost only in the highest volume case.
examples.zh: 预测只在产量最高的情景下加入了「增开班次成本」。

examples.en: Our class separated additional shift cost from wages for the normal shift.
examples.zh: 全班把「增开班次成本」和常规班次的工资分开了。

collocations: a worksheet with additional shift cost

words.enDefinition: a reported per-share result using earnings that include stated adjustments

examples.en: The sample table listed adjusted earnings per share beside the reported figure for the same year.
examples.zh: 样本表在同一年的列报数据旁列出了「调整后每股收益」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the share count used for adjusted earnings per share had also changed.
examples.zh: 导师问，计算「调整后每股收益」所用的股数是否也发生了变动。

collocations: a reconciliation of adjusted earnings per share

words.zhGloss: 调整后息税折旧摊销前利润
words.enDefinition: EBITDA modified by additional adjustments specified by its presenter
acceptedZhAnswers: 调整后息税折旧摊销前利润

examples.en: The sample release stated exactly which items management excluded when calculating adjusted EBITDA.
examples.zh: 样本公告明确列出了管理层在计算「调整后息税折旧摊销前利润」时剔除的项目。

examples.en: We read the definition of adjusted EBITDA before comparing it with the previous year's figure.
examples.zh: 我们先阅读了「调整后息税折旧摊销前利润」的定义，再与上年数字作比较。

words.enDefinition: net income modified by stated adjustments for analysis or disclosure

examples.en: The fictional company's adjusted net income reflected a stated tax effect for each excluded charge.
examples.zh: 虚构公司的「调整后净利润」反映了各项剔除费用的税务影响。

examples.en: We checked whether adjusted net income and reported earnings moved in the same direction.
examples.zh: 我们核对了「调整后净利润」和列报盈利的变动方向是否相同。

collocations: a reconciliation of adjusted net income

words.enDefinition: an operating profit margin calculated using stated adjustments

examples.en: The exercise divided adjusted operating profit by the stated revenue to find the adjusted operating margin.
examples.zh: 练习用调整后营业利润除以列示收入，得出「调整后营业利润率」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why the adjusted operating margin changed less than the reported margin in the table.
examples.zh: 导师问，为什么表里「调整后营业利润率」的变动小于报告利润率。

words.enDefinition: operating profit after specified adjustments in a supplementary measure

examples.en: The sample reconciled adjusted operating profit to the amount shown in its main income statement.
examples.zh: 样本将「调整后营业利润」调节至利润表主表中的金额。

examples.en: We examined whether the same costs were excluded from adjusted operating profit in both years.
examples.zh: 我们检查两年计算「调整后营业利润」时剔除的成本是否相同。

words.enDefinition: An event after the period providing evidence of a condition that already existed at the reporting date.

examples.en: The case treated the court decision as an adjusting event because the underlying dispute existed at year end.
examples.zh: 例题把法院判决作为「日后调整事项」，因为相关争议在年末已经存在。

examples.en: The later inventory sale was an adjusting event because it confirmed the condition of inventory at year end.
examples.zh: 后续存货销售印证了年末存货的状况，因此属于「日后调整事项」。

collocations: recognise the effect of an adjusting event
treat later evidence as an adjusting event

words.enDefinition: a change made in a cash flow reconciliation to remove effects that did not move cash

examples.en: The largest adjustment for non-cash items reversed the depreciation charge before the total was calculated.
examples.zh: 计算合计之前，金额最大的「非现金项目调整」加回了折旧费用。

examples.en: An adjustment for non-cash items removed the gain arising from remeasuring the liability at year end.
examples.zh: 通过一项「非现金项目调整」，剔除了年末重新计量该负债所产生的收益。

collocations: make an adjustment for non-cash items
calculate an adjustment for non-cash items
show the adjustment for non-cash items

words.enDefinition: a change removing an exchange loss recognised in the starting profit subtotal before cash settlement

examples.en: The adjustment for unrealised exchange losses removed the effect of remeasuring a foreign currency payable before settlement.
examples.zh: 「未实现汇兑损失调整」剔除了外币应付款在结算前重新计量的影响。

examples.en: In the example, an adjustment for unrealised exchange losses left the foreign currency cash balance unchanged.
examples.zh: 示例作了「未实现汇兑损失调整」，外币现金余额没有因此变化。

collocations: make an adjustment for unrealised exchange losses
calculate the adjustment for unrealised exchange losses
review the adjustment for unrealised exchange losses

words.enDefinition: A change to balances at the start of a presented period, such as for a retrospective correction.

examples.en: The notes explained an adjustment to opening balances because the error predated both of the years presented.
examples.zh: 差错发生在列报的两个年度之前，附注因此解释了一项「期初余额调整」。

examples.en: We located the adjustment to opening balances in the equity statement before checking the accounting policy note.
examples.zh: 我们先在权益变动表找到「期初余额调整」，再检查会计政策附注。

collocations: record an adjustment to opening balances
explain an adjustment to opening balances
show the adjustment to opening balances in equity

words.enDefinition: an adjustment calculated after allowing for its tax effect

examples.en: The sample table reported an after-tax adjustment before arriving at the fictional company's adjusted net income.
examples.zh: 样本表在算出虚构公司的调整后净利润之前，列出了一个「税后调整额」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how the after-tax adjustment differed from the amount shown before tax.
examples.zh: 导师问，「税后调整额」与税前列示的金额有什么区别。

words.enDefinition: Combining items with shared characteristics into a single total or group in financial reporting.

examples.en: The report used aggregation for several small costs that shared the same nature in the example.
examples.zh: 示例报告对几项性质相同的小额费用作了「汇总列报」。

examples.en: Our group discussed whether further aggregation would make the main statement easier to read in this case.
examples.zh: 我们组讨论了在本例中进一步「汇总列报」会不会让主表更易读。

words.enDefinition: a share of a cost assigned to a cost object according to a chosen allocation method

examples.en: The allocated cost for the weekend class included its share of the studio's monthly rent.
examples.zh: 周末课程「分摊后计入的成本」包括它应承担的那部分月租。

examples.en: We compared the allocated cost for two activities that used the same workshop on different days.
examples.zh: 我们比较了在不同日期用同一间工作室的两项活动各自「分摊后计入的成本」。

words.enDefinition: The measure used to apportion shared expenses among participating units

examples.en: The case used floor area as its allocation basis for shared costs for the two units.
examples.zh: 案例用占地面积作为两个单位的「共同成本分摊依据」。

examples.en: We tested a different allocation basis for shared costs and compared the resulting reports.
examples.zh: 我们试用了不同的「共同成本分摊依据」，对比了生成的报告。

collocations: choose an allocation basis for shared costs
change the allocation basis for shared costs
explain an allocation basis for shared costs

words.enDefinition: the order in which different groups of costs are assigned

examples.en: We changed the allocation sequence to see how it affected the cost charged to printing.
examples.zh: 我们调整了「分配顺序」，观察它如何影响计入印刷部门的成本。

examples.en: The workbook showed the allocation sequence for support departments before listing the final assigned costs.
examples.zh: 练习册先展示辅助部门的「分配顺序」，再列出最终分配的成本。

words.enDefinition: a financial measure outside those defined by the applicable reporting framework

examples.en: The European sample report described why management used an alternative performance measure in its commentary.
examples.zh: 欧洲样本报告在管理层评论中解释了管理层使用「替代性业绩指标」的原因。

examples.en: We checked how the alternative performance measure had been calculated before comparing the fictional companies.
examples.zh: 比较虚构公司之前，我们核对了「替代性业绩指标」是怎么计算的。

words.enDefinition: an increase in the indirect reconciliation that removes the effect of amortisation expense from the starting profit subtotal

examples.en: The amortisation add-back removed the software licence amortisation expense from the indirect cash flow calculation.
examples.zh: 「摊销加回」使软件许可摊销费用不再影响间接法的现金流计算。

examples.en: The optional schedule listed the amortisation add-back separately from adjustments for changes in trade receivables.
examples.zh: 选用的附表把「摊销加回」与应收账款变动的调整分开列示。

words.enDefinition: to express shorter-period figures on an annual basis

examples.en: The worksheet asked us to annualise the figures before comparing amounts stated on different time bases.
examples.zh: 练习表要求我们先「将数字年化」，再比较按不同时间口径列示的金额。

examples.en: The tutor showed why we should state the assumptions whenever we annualise the figures.
examples.zh: 导师说明了每次「将数字年化」时为什么要交代所用假设。

collocations: annualise the figures using a stated assumption
annualise the figures from a short period

words.enDefinition: the overhead charged to jobs or output using an allocation rate

examples.en: The applied overhead on the repair job depended on how many machine hours were recorded.
examples.zh: 维修作业的「已分配间接费用」取决于记录了多少机器工时。

examples.en: We compared applied overhead with the total overhead actually incurred during the same month.
examples.zh: 我们把「已分配间接费用」与同月实际发生的间接费用总额作了比较。

collocations: compare applied overhead with actual overhead

words.enDefinition: Terms comparable to those that independent parties would agree to under similar circumstances.

examples.en: The class compared the sister company's rental agreement with independent leases when discussing arm's length terms.
examples.zh: 全班讨论「公平交易条款」时，把同一集团内公司的租赁协议与独立各方之间的租约作了比较。

examples.en: Our tutor asked what evidence would support the claim that the loan was made on arm's length terms.
examples.zh: 老师问，什么证据可以支持该贷款是按「公平交易条款」发放的说法。

words.enDefinition: an asset received before the buyer pays the amount owed for it

examples.en: The case disclosed an asset acquired on credit that remained unpaid when the reporting period ended.
examples.zh: 案例披露了一项「赊购取得的资产」，报告期结束时，公司仍未付清该资产的款项。

examples.en: We found the asset acquired on credit in the equipment note before tracing its later cash payment.
examples.zh: 我们先在设备附注里找到了这项「赊购取得的资产」，再追溯其后续付款。

collocations: disclose an asset acquired on credit
record an asset acquired on credit
pay for an asset acquired on credit

words.enDefinition: agreeing or becoming obliged to take on liabilities that were previously borne by someone else

examples.en: The buyer's assumption of liabilities was disclosed alongside the purchase price in the example's acquisition note.
examples.zh: 示例的收购附注在列示购买价的同时披露了买方的「承接负债」安排。

examples.en: The transaction involved the assumption of liabilities for equipment financing that had originally belonged to the seller.
examples.zh: 这笔交易涉及「承接负债」，即把原由卖方承担的设备融资债务接过来。

collocations: account for the assumption of liabilities
agree to the assumption of liabilities

words.enDefinition: Formally approved for release by the body responsible for giving that approval.

examples.en: The sample financial statements were authorised for issue two weeks before they were published on the website.
examples.zh: 示例财务报表在网站公开前两周已「获准报出」。

examples.en: The note named the body that approved the financial statements and said when they were authorised for issue.
examples.zh: 附注写明了批准财务报表的机构，以及报表何时「获准报出」。

collocations: the date the accounts were authorised for issue
before the statements were authorised for issue

words.enDefinition: The average recorded value of assets used in operating activities

examples.en: We calculated average operating assets from the opening and closing figures in the case.
examples.zh: 我们使用案例中的期初和期末数据计算「平均经营资产」。

examples.en: The worksheet listed average operating assets beneath the line for operating profit.
examples.zh: 练习表在营业利润一行下面列了「平均经营资产」。

words.enDefinition: the average amount owed to suppliers during the measured period

examples.en: The sample worksheet estimated the average payables balance from two figures shown on the balance sheet.
examples.zh: 样本练习表用资产负债表上列出的两个数字来估算「平均应付账款余额」。

examples.en: We checked which supplier balances counted toward the average payables balance for the case.
examples.zh: 我们核对了哪些供应商余额计入案例的「平均应付账款余额」。

words.enDefinition: the average amount customers owe during a measured period

examples.en: The class used an average receivables balance instead of the single year-end figure in the comparison.
examples.zh: 在比较中，同学们采用「平均应收账款余额」，没有只用年末数字。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how seasonal sales affected the average receivables balance in the sample.
examples.zh: 导师问，季节性销售如何影响样本的「平均应收账款余额」。

words.enDefinition: the average shareholders' equity balance over the period analysed

examples.en: We used average shareholders' equity to account for the midyear change in the sample company's balance.
examples.zh: 样本公司的余额在年中发生变化，我们用「平均股东权益」来反映这一变化。

examples.en: The worksheet calculated average shareholders' equity from the beginning and ending amounts in the case.
examples.zh: 练习表用案例中的期初和期末金额计算「平均股东权益」。

collocations: a return on average shareholders' equity

words.enDefinition: the average total asset balance used for a period

examples.en: The course exercise averaged the opening and closing balances to calculate average total assets.
examples.zh: 课程练习用期初和期末余额的平均数计算「平均总资产」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why average total assets could differ from the figure shown at year end.
examples.zh: 导师问，「平均总资产」为何可能与年末数字不同。

collocations: use average total assets as the denominator

words.zhGloss: 调拨可节省的对外销售费
words.enDefinition: External selling expenses saved when goods are transferred within the organisation
acceptedZhAnswers: 调拨可节省的对外销售费

examples.en: The model deducted avoidable external selling costs before using the market price as a reference.
examples.zh: 模型先扣除「调拨可节省的对外销售费」，再以市场价为参考。

examples.en: The sales commission was among the avoidable external selling costs in our classroom case.
examples.zh: 在课堂案例里，销售佣金属于「调拨可节省的对外销售费」。

words.enDefinition: Facilities expense that ends when a particular activity or site closes

examples.en: The cancelled storage lease counted as avoidable facility cost in the closure analysis.
examples.zh: 在关闭分析中，取消的仓储租赁费计入「可节省的设施成本」。

examples.en: We calculated avoidable facility cost separately from rent that the business still paid.
examples.zh: 我们把「可节省的设施成本」与企业仍要支付的租金分开计算。

words.zhGloss: 可节省的内部生产成本
words.enDefinition: Internal costs that would stop if work moved to a supplier
acceptedZhAnswers: 可节省的内部生产成本

examples.en: The case listed avoidable in-house costs that would disappear if we outsourced the parts.
examples.zh: 案例列出了外包零件后可以省掉的「内部生产成本」。

examples.en: We compared avoidable in-house costs with the supplier's price and extra delivery expense.
examples.zh: 我们把「可节省的内部生产成本」同供应商报价及额外配送费进行了比较。

collocations: compare avoidable in-house costs with the quote

words.enDefinition: Payroll spending that would end if a specific activity stopped

examples.en: The tutor listed temporary shifts under avoidable payroll cost for the closure decision.
examples.zh: 导师在关闭决定的练习中，把临时班次列为「可节省的薪资成本」。

examples.en: We separated the avoidable payroll cost from salaries the workshop would continue paying.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「可节省的薪资成本」与工作室仍会支付的工资。

words.expression: bank overdraft integral to cash management
words.lemma: bank overdraft integral to cash management
words.zhGloss: 现金管理不可分割的银行透支
words.enDefinition: an overdraft used routinely in managing cash that may count within IAS 7 cash and cash equivalents if repayable on demand
acceptedZhAnswers: 现金管理不可分割的银行透支
acceptedEnVariants: bank overdraft integral to cash management

examples.en: The IAS 7 example included a bank overdraft integral to cash management in its cash and cash equivalents.
examples.zh: IAS 7 示例把一项「现金管理不可分割的银行透支」计入现金及现金等价物。

examples.en: The note explained how a bank overdraft integral to cash management fluctuated between positive and negative balances.
examples.zh: 附注解释了「现金管理不可分割的银行透支」涉及的账户如何在正余额和负余额之间波动。

collocations: disclose a bank overdraft integral to cash management
identify a bank overdraft integral to cash management
include a bank overdraft integral to cash management

words.enDefinition: the influence of the comparison period's level on measured growth

examples.en: The tutor used a base effect to explain the large increase from an unusually weak prior-year quarter.
examples.zh: 导师用「基数效应」解释，为什么去年同期表现疲软时，本期的增长数字看起来很高。

examples.en: We identified a base effect because the earlier figures included several weeks with the store closed.
examples.zh: 此前的数据涵盖商店关门的几周，我们据此发现了「基数效应」。

words.enDefinition: the reference period against which other periods are compared

examples.en: We chose 2022 as the base period because the sample had a complete year of data.
examples.zh: 我们选二〇二二年为「基期」，因为样本有该年的完整数据。

examples.en: Changing the base period altered the index values on the chart without changing the original amounts.
examples.zh: 更换「基期」改变了图上的指数值，原来的金额保持不变。

words.enDefinition: an index that sets a reference year's value to 100

examples.en: The base-year index let us plot sales and staffing costs on the same chart.
examples.zh: 「基年指数」让我们能把销售额和人工成本放在同一张图里。

examples.en: We calculated the base-year index after choosing a year with complete figures for every business unit.
examples.zh: 我们选了一年各业务单位数据都齐全的年份，再计算「基年指数」。

collocations: compare figures using a base-year index

words.enDefinition: the method and conventions used to obtain a stated amount

examples.en: The sample disclosed the basis of calculation for both the operating margin and adjusted earnings.
examples.zh: 样本披露了营业利润率和调整后盈利的「计算口径」。

examples.en: We compared the basis of calculation in the footnotes before aligning the two companies' ratios.
examples.zh: 我们先比较了脚注里的「计算口径」，再统一两家公司的比率口径。

words.enDefinition: The reporting framework and conventions used to prepare a set of financial statements.

examples.en: We checked the basis of preparation before comparing the example statements with a company reporting under different standards.
examples.zh: 在把示例财务报表与采用不同准则的公司作比较前，我们先核对了「财务报表编制基础」。

examples.en: The basis of preparation explained which reporting framework the group used for its consolidated statements.
examples.zh: 「财务报表编制基础」说明了集团用哪套报告框架来编制合并报表。

words.enDefinition: a difference expressed in hundredths of a percentage point

examples.en: The worksheet used a basis-point change to express a small increase in the operating margin.
examples.zh: 练习表用「基点变动」表示营业利润率的小幅上升。

examples.en: The recorded basis-point change was one hundred when the margins differed by one percentage point.
examples.zh: 两项利润率相差一个百分点，记录的「基点变动」为一百个基点。

words.enDefinition: a method assigning costs to a batch of identical or similar items, often to calculate the unit cost

examples.en: We applied batch costing to estimate the production cost of one notebook in the latest batch.
examples.zh: 我们用「按批核算成本」估算最新一批笔记本中一本的生产成本。

examples.en: The workbook explained batch costing using several identical kits prepared together for the course.
examples.zh: 练习册用为课程一起准备的几套相同用具讲解「按批核算成本」。

words.enDefinition: an activity undertaken for a batch regardless of how many units it contains

examples.en: Changing the printing plates was a batch-level activity because we did it once for each batch.
examples.zh: 更换印版是「批次级作业」，因为每批只换一次。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether checking the batch setup counted as a batch-level activity in the case.
examples.zh: 讲师问，核查批次准备在案例中是否算「批次级作业」。

words.enDefinition: unfinished units already in production at the start of a period, or their recorded inventory cost

examples.en: The exercise included beginning work in process from orders that were started the previous month.
examples.zh: 练习纳入了上个月已开始生产的订单中的「期初在产品」。

examples.en: We calculated how much additional work the beginning work in process needed before it was finished.
examples.zh: 我们算了「期初在产品」在完工前还需要多少加工。

collocations: cost of beginning work in process

words.enDefinition: Under IAS 37, the amount that best reflects what settling or transferring the obligation would cost at the reporting date.

examples.en: The warranty example used recent claims experience to develop the best estimate of costs for products already sold.
examples.zh: 保修例题依据近期索赔情况，得出已售产品预计赔付成本的「最佳估计数」。

examples.en: We compared the best estimate with the amounts in the sample note to understand how uncertainty was reported.
examples.zh: 我们用「最佳估计数」对照示例附注里的金额，了解报告如何说明不确定性。

collocations: review the best estimate for a provision
use the best estimate of settlement costs

words.enDefinition: recognising unusually large charges in one period to improve the appearance of later results

examples.en: The case discussion considered big bath accounting after several unusually large charges appeared together.
examples.zh: 案例讨论涉及「大洗澡式会计处理」，当时有几笔异常大的支出同时列报。

examples.en: Our tutor distinguished suspected big bath accounting from a single period of genuine deterioration.
examples.zh: 导师区分了疑似「大洗澡式会计处理」和某一期经营状况的实际恶化。

words.enDefinition: The output or available time at the operation limiting total production

examples.en: The two products shared the same bottleneck capacity on the finishing machine.
examples.zh: 两款产品共用收尾设备这道工序的「瓶颈工序产能」。

examples.en: Cleaning reduced bottleneck capacity by taking time away from the limiting machine.
examples.zh: 清洁占用了瓶颈机器的运行时间，使「瓶颈工序产能」下降。

collocations: make better use of bottleneck capacity

words.enDefinition: Minutes available or required at the operation limiting total output

examples.en: The first product used more bottleneck minutes even though it was smaller.
examples.zh: 第一款产品虽较小，却占用了更多「瓶颈工序分钟数」。

examples.en: We checked the available bottleneck minutes before completing the sample production plan.
examples.zh: 我们先核对了可用的「瓶颈工序分钟数」，再完成示例生产计划。

words.enDefinition: An approach in which lower-level units prepare estimates that are reviewed and combined at higher levels.

examples.en: The university theatre used bottom-up budgeting so each team estimated the costs of its own events.
examples.zh: 大学剧院采用「自下而上的预算编制」，由各团队估算各自的活动成本。

examples.en: With bottom-up budgeting, we combined workshop estimates before discussing the figures with the department manager.
examples.zh: 在「自下而上的预算编制」中，我们先汇总工场的估算，再和部门经理讨论数字。

words.enDefinition: To divide a difference into components showing the individual changes that account for it.

examples.en: The tutor asked us to break down a variance instead of giving the class one unexplained total.
examples.zh: 老师让我们「分解差异」，别只给全班一个没有解释的总数。

examples.en: To break down a variance, our group needed sales quantities and the unit price for each product.
examples.zh: 要「分解差异」，我们组需要每件商品的销量和单价。

collocations: break down a variance by product
break down a variance into price and volume
break down a variance for the report

words.enDefinition: Being answerable for commitments and results within an assigned budget and for explaining departures from it.

examples.en: Budget accountability in the case meant explaining unexpected expenses and showing how the team used its allocation.
examples.zh: 案例里的「预算问责」要求解释意外支出，并说明团队如何使用分配到的经费。

examples.en: The tutor asked how budget accountability would work when two departments used the same pool of funds.
examples.zh: 老师问，两个部门使用同一笔经费时，如何落实「预算问责」。

collocations: define budget accountability for each unit

words.enDefinition: Estimates or assumptions about future conditions used to construct the budget.

examples.en: The budget assumptions included similar ticket demand on both weekends, even though the sessions differed.
examples.zh: 「预算编制假设」包括，尽管两个周末的场次不同，门票需求大致相同。

examples.en: We recorded our budget assumptions before asking the coordinator to check the planned staffing costs.
examples.zh: 请协调员核对计划人员成本前，我们记录了「预算编制假设」。

words.enDefinition: A schedule showing when estimates, revisions, reviews, and approvals are due during budget preparation.

examples.en: The budget calendar gave each department a week to revise its figures after the first review.
examples.zh: 「预算编制日程」给各部门留了一周，在初审之后修改数字。

examples.en: We checked the budget calendar before arranging to discuss the workshop's planned purchases with the manager.
examples.zh: 和经理约时间讨论工场计划采购之前，我们先查看了「预算编制日程」。

words.enDefinition: a limit on how much spending may be included in or authorised under a budget for a unit or purpose

examples.en: The workshop's budget ceiling limited how much the student team could plan to spend on tools.
examples.zh: 工场的「预算支出上限」限制了学生团队可以为工具编列多少费用。

examples.en: We checked the budget ceiling before choosing which repairs to include in the next period.
examples.zh: 确定下一期包含哪些维修之前，我们先核对了「预算支出上限」。

words.enDefinition: Adherence to the spending limits, authorisations and other requirements of an approved budget.

examples.en: The case assigned budget compliance to the office manager, who checked workshop orders against approved spending categories.
examples.zh: 案例由行政经理负责「预算执行合规性」，核查工场订单是否属于经批准的支出类别。

examples.en: The review looked at budget compliance because two projects had moved spending between categories without approval.
examples.zh: 有两个项目未经批准就在不同类别之间调剂了支出，所以审查关注「预算执行合规性」。

collocations: check budget compliance before approving a purchase

words.enDefinition: A temporary restriction on changing budgets or authorising additional spending, depending on the organisation's rules.

examples.en: The example department faced a budget freeze while administrators reviewed spending on the new equipment.
examples.zh: 管理人员审查新设备支出期间，例子中的部门面临「预算冻结」。

examples.en: The supervisor explained which routine purchases could still go ahead during the temporary budget freeze.
examples.zh: 主管解释了临时「预算冻结」期间，哪些日常采购仍然可以进行。

collocations: review the effect of a budget freeze

words.enDefinition: Instructions or assumptions given to the people preparing budgets so they use a consistent basis.

examples.en: The budget guidance asked every workshop to explain any increase in expected material usage next year.
examples.zh: 「预算编制指引」要求各工场解释下一年预计材料用量增加的原因。

examples.en: Our group checked the budget guidance before estimating how much power the new printer would use.
examples.zh: 估算新打印机的用电量前，我们小组先看了「预算编制指引」。

words.enDefinition: A meeting to examine a budget proposal or figures and discuss any changes needed.

examples.en: At the budget review meeting, two departments explained why their staffing estimates had changed.
examples.zh: 在「预算审查会议」上，两个部门解释了人手估算为什么变了。

examples.en: We brought the sales assumptions to the budget review meeting so the group could check them.
examples.zh: 我们把销售假设带到「预算审查会议」上，让小组核对。

collocations: prepare for the budget review meeting
present figures at a budget review meeting

words.enDefinition: The amount by which expected or available resources fall short of what the budget needs to cover planned costs.

examples.en: The budget shortfall arose when the case assumed the project would receive less funding for campus workshops.
examples.zh: 案例预计校园工场项目获得的经费会减少，因此出现了「预算资金缺口」。

examples.en: We used the revised grant figure to estimate the budget shortfall before writing our classroom report.
examples.zh: 写课堂报告前，我们用修订后的资助金额估算了「预算资金缺口」。

collocations: explain the budget shortfall in the report

words.enDefinition: Extra room deliberately built into a budget by overstating needs or understating expected performance.

examples.en: The case asked whether the extra labour allowance represented budget slack or a realistic estimate.
examples.zh: 案例问，多留的人工额度是「预算松弛」，还是依据实际情况作出的估算。

examples.en: We looked for budget slack after seeing that all three teams had understated their expected sales.
examples.zh: 我们看到三个团队都低报了预期销售额，便核查是否存在「预算松弛」。

words.enDefinition: A set of budget figures and supporting information sent to someone for review or approval.

examples.en: Our budget submission included the expected attendance and the cost of running each student workshop.
examples.zh: 我们「提交的预算材料」包括预计到场人数和举办每场学生工作坊的成本。

examples.en: The manager returned the budget submission because one page omitted the assumptions about weekend staffing.
examples.zh: 有一页没写周末人手安排的假设，经理退回了「提交的预算材料」。

words.enDefinition: A stated level of revenue, cost, or other performance to be achieved under a budget.

examples.en: The finance team set a budget target for postage based on the mailing schedule for the term.
examples.zh: 财务团队根据本学期的邮寄安排，设定了邮费「预算目标」。

examples.en: We compared the actual repairs completed with the budget target for the workshop's first month.
examples.zh: 我们把实际完成的维修量与工场首月的「预算目标」作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A difference arising because a planned income or expense item falls into a different budget period than expected.

examples.en: The tutor called it a budget timing variance because the planned service happened a month later.
examples.zh: 老师说这是「预算时间性差异」，因为原计划的服务晚了一个月才发生。

examples.en: A budget timing variance appeared in May and reversed when the planned service took place in June.
examples.zh: 五月出现了「预算时间性差异」，六月原定的服务实际发生后，这项差异随之抵消。

collocations: track the reversal of a budget timing variance

words.zhGloss: 预算与最新预测的比较
words.enDefinition: A comparison of the approved plan with the latest estimate of where the period's results will end up.
acceptedZhAnswers: 预算与最新预测的比较

examples.en: The budget-to-forecast comparison showed that recent paper price changes could put the print room above its spending plan.
examples.zh: 「预算与最新预测的比较」显示，最近纸价的变化可能使印刷室开支超出计划。

examples.en: Our group used a budget-to-forecast comparison to explain why the annual repairs estimate had changed since approval.
examples.zh: 我们组用「预算与最新预测的比较」，解释年度维修费估计为何在预算批准后发生变化。

collocations: show expected changes in a budget-to-forecast comparison

words.enDefinition: The number of labour or machine hours included in the budget for an activity or period.

examples.en: The case gave us budgeted activity hours for the press and separate hours for the finishing bench.
examples.zh: 案例给出了印刷机的「预算作业工时」，并另外列了后加工台的工时。

examples.en: We compared actual machine time with budgeted activity hours before working out the fixed overhead capacity variance.
examples.zh: 我们先对比实际机器工时与「预算作业工时」，再计算固定制造费用产能差异。

collocations: base overhead rates on budgeted activity hours
compare actual hours with budgeted activity hours

words.enDefinition: The expected cash at the end of a budget period after planned receipts, payments and any financing cash flows.

examples.en: The budgeted ending cash balance for June became the starting figure in the next month's worksheet.
examples.zh: 六月的「预计期末现金余额」成为下个月练习表的期初数字。

examples.en: We checked the budgeted ending cash balance after subtracting the planned payment for the new projector.
examples.zh: 扣除计划支付的新投影仪款后，我们核对了「预计期末现金余额」。

collocations: calculate the budgeted ending cash balance
carry forward the budgeted ending cash balance
check the budgeted ending cash balance

words.enDefinition: The planned proportions of different products in total unit sales for the period.

examples.en: The budgeted sales mix was two plain notebooks for every one with a printed cover in our exercise.
examples.zh: 练习的「预算销售组合」是每卖出两本素面笔记本，就卖出一本印花封面的。

examples.en: We applied the budgeted sales mix to the total units sold before measuring the quantity effect.
examples.zh: 我们把「预算销售组合」应用到总销量上，再计算数量影响。

collocations: compare actual sales with the budgeted sales mix
hold the budgeted sales mix constant

words.enDefinition: The selling price assumed for one unit when preparing the sales budget.

examples.en: The budgeted selling price stayed unchanged when the student group revised its estimate of ticket sales.
examples.zh: 学生小组更新门票销量估计值时，「预算销售单价」仍保持原值。

examples.en: We compared the budgeted selling price with what customers actually paid during the sample period.
examples.zh: 我们把「预算销售单价」与示例期间顾客实际支付的单价作了比较。

collocations: compare actual prices with the budgeted selling price

words.enDefinition: The number of units that the organisation expects to sell in the budget period.

examples.en: We multiplied budgeted unit sales by the expected price to estimate revenue for the print stall.
examples.zh: 我们把「预算销量」乘以预计价格，估算印刷摊位的收入。

examples.en: The team reduced budgeted unit sales after learning that one branch would close during the holidays.
examples.zh: 得知一个分点假期会关闭后，团队调低了「预算销量」。

words.enDefinition: The business unit receiving goods or services in an internal transfer

examples.en: The buying division compared the internal charge with the outside quote.
examples.zh: 「内部采购分部」比较了内部收费与外部报价。

examples.en: In the sample accounts, the buying division recorded a component cost.
examples.zh: 在账户样本里，「内部采购分部」记录了一笔零件成本。

collocations: compare options for the buying division
costs recorded by the buying division

words.enDefinition: an output from a process with relatively minor value compared with its main products

examples.en: The worksheet treated the small wood offcuts as a by-product of making the shelves.
examples.zh: 练习表把做架子剩下的小块木料列为「副产品」。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked how revenue from the by-product would appear in the production report.
examples.zh: 讲师问，「副产品」收入会怎样显示在生产报告中。

words.zhGloss: 按自然期间对齐的财务数据
words.enDefinition: financial amounts adjusted to cover common calendar dates so entities with different fiscal periods can be compared
acceptedZhAnswers: 按自然期间对齐的财务数据

examples.en: We used calendarised figures to compare two retailers whose financial years ended in different months.
examples.zh: 我们用「按自然期间对齐的财务数据」比较两家财年在不同月份结束的零售商。

examples.en: The worksheet presented calendarised figures after combining the relevant months from each company's annual and interim reports.
examples.zh: 练习表汇总了各公司年报和中报中相关月份的数据，列出「按自然期间对齐的财务数据」。

words.enDefinition: the cost of supplying a resource divided by the practical capacity it makes available

examples.en: We divided the cost of the support team by its practical hours to find the capacity cost rate.
examples.zh: 我们用支持团队的总成本除以实际可用工时，得出「单位产能成本率」。

examples.en: The capacity cost rate was expressed in pounds per available hour in the workshop example.
examples.zh: 工作室示例里的「单位产能成本率」用每可用小时多少英镑来表示。

words.enDefinition: Production capacity no longer needed after work is assigned externally

examples.en: The worksheet estimated capacity freed by outsourcing before considering an alternative batch of work.
examples.zh: 练习表先估算「外包后腾出的产能」，之后才考虑是否改做另一批业务。

examples.en: Our case used capacity freed by outsourcing to make presses available for another product.
examples.zh: 案例通过「外包后腾出的产能」，让印刷机可用于另一款产品。

words.enDefinition: the amount of productive capacity made available by the resources an organisation has provided

examples.en: We compared capacity supplied with the actual processing time used by the returns department last month.
examples.zh: 我们将「资源供给产能」与退货部门上个月的实际处理时间作了比较。

examples.en: Adding another shift increased capacity supplied even though demand for the service did not immediately change.
examples.zh: 尽管服务需求没有立即变化，多排一个班次增加了「资源供给产能」。

collocations: measure capacity supplied in labour hours
compare capacity supplied with capacity used

words.enDefinition: how effectively a business uses capital to generate operating results

examples.en: The case compared capital efficiency at two factories with similar output but different equipment investments.
examples.zh: 案例比较了两家产量相近、设备投入不同的工厂的「资本使用效率」。

examples.en: Our report examined capital efficiency before and after the fictional retailer closed an unused warehouse.
examples.zh: 报告考察了虚构零售商关闭闲置仓库前后的「资本使用效率」。

words.enDefinition: development costs included in the carrying amount of an asset after the recognition criteria have been met

examples.en: The note separated capitalised development expenditure from research costs expensed in the year they were incurred.
examples.zh: 附注将「资本化的开发支出」与发生当年计入费用的研究成本分开。

examples.en: The example listed payments for capitalised development expenditure as investing cash flows when creating the new asset.
examples.zh: 示例将形成新资产时支付的「资本化的开发支出」列为投资现金流。

collocations: cash paid for capitalised development expenditure

words.zhGloss: 资本化利息相关现金流
words.enDefinition: cash payments of interest that has been included in the cost of a qualifying asset
acceptedZhAnswers: 资本化利息相关现金流

examples.en: The example discussed capitalised interest cash flows after showing the interest included in the new asset's carrying amount.
examples.zh: 示例先展示了纳入新资产账面价值的利息，再讨论「资本化利息相关现金流」。

examples.en: We checked the disclosure for capitalised interest cash flows against the interest payments recorded during construction.
examples.zh: 我们用施工期间记录的利息付款核对了「资本化利息相关现金流」披露。

words.expression: carrying amount of supplier finance liabilities
words.lemma: carrying amount of supplier finance liabilities
words.zhGloss: 供应商融资负债的账面金额
words.enDefinition: the amount at which liabilities included in a supplier finance arrangement are reported in the statement of financial position
acceptedZhAnswers: 供应商融资负债的账面金额
acceptedEnVariants: carrying amount of supplier finance liabilities

examples.en: The note showed the carrying amount of supplier finance liabilities at the beginning and end of the period.
examples.zh: 附注列出了期初和期末的「供应商融资负债的账面金额」。

examples.en: We traced the carrying amount of supplier finance liabilities to the relevant line items in the balance sheet.
examples.zh: 我们在资产负债表上找到了与「供应商融资负债的账面金额」对应的项目。

collocations: disclose the carrying amount of supplier finance liabilities
calculate the carrying amount of supplier finance liabilities
reconcile the carrying amount of supplier finance liabilities

words.enDefinition: the amount of cash taken up by an activity or balance increase

examples.en: The exercise attributed cash absorption to the retailer's larger stock position at the end of term.
examples.zh: 练习将「现金占用」归因于零售商学期末存货增加。

examples.en: We calculated cash absorption from changes in the operating balances shown in the sample table.
examples.zh: 我们根据样本表中经营性余额的变化计算了「现金占用」。

collocations: a temporary rise in cash absorption

words.enDefinition: cash and cash equivalent balances held by a business when the reporting entity obtains control of it

examples.en: The amount of cash acquired reduced the net cash outflow presented for the purchase of the subsidiary.
examples.zh: 「取得的现金」金额减少了报表中购买子公司一项列示的现金净流出。

examples.en: We checked cash acquired against the acquisition date figures in the supplemental schedule provided with the case.
examples.zh: 我们根据案例补充附表中取得日的数字核对了「取得的现金」。

collocations: report the amount of cash acquired

words.zhGloss: 向外部各方垫付的现金
words.enDefinition: cash paid out as loans or advances to other individuals or organisations
acceptedZhAnswers: 向外部各方垫付的现金

examples.en: The model statement listed cash advanced to other parties after the company made a loan to an affiliate.
examples.zh: 示例报表在公司向关联方发放贷款后列出了「向外部各方垫付的现金」。

examples.en: The note distinguished cash advanced to other parties from cash already received on earlier loans.
examples.zh: 附注把「向外部各方垫付的现金」与先前贷款已收回的现金区分开来。

collocations: report cash advanced to other parties
disclose cash advanced to other parties
reconcile cash advanced to other parties

words.enDefinition: cash on hand, demand deposits and qualifying highly liquid short-term investments

examples.en: We traced cash and cash equivalents from the balance sheet to the statement's closing total.
examples.zh: 我们把资产负债表上的「现金及现金等价物」追溯到现金流量表的期末合计。

examples.en: The note listed the accounts and short-term investments included in cash and cash equivalents at year end.
examples.zh: 附注列出了年末计入「现金及现金等价物」的各账户和短期投资。

collocations: components of cash and cash equivalents

words.enDefinition: reported earnings supported by actual cash generation

examples.en: In the sample, rising operating cash flows supported earnings growth, suggesting cash-backed earnings.
examples.zh: 样本中的经营现金流增长支持了利润增长，显示盈利可能「有现金支撑」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked what other information was needed before calling the result cash-backed earnings.
examples.zh: 讲师问，还需要哪些信息才能把这个结果称为「有现金支撑的盈利」。

words.enDefinition: The projected period-end cash after nonfinancing receipts and payments, before borrowing or other financing flows.

examples.en: We calculated the cash balance before financing by adding receipts and subtracting payments from the opening balance.
examples.zh: 我们从期初余额加上收款、扣除付款，求出「融资前现金余额」。

examples.en: The case compared the cash balance before financing with the minimum balance the bookshop wanted to maintain.
examples.zh: 案例把「融资前现金余额」与书店想保持的最低余额作了比较。

collocations: calculate the cash balance before financing
show the cash balance before financing
compare the cash balance before financing with the target

words.zhGloss: 筹资活动产生的负债的现金变动
words.enDefinition: movements in financing-related liabilities resulting from receipts or payments of cash
acceptedZhAnswers: 筹资活动产生的负债的现金变动

examples.en: We tracked cash changes in financing liabilities by matching loan drawdowns and principal repayments to the bank records.
examples.zh: 我们将贷款提款和本金偿还与银行记录相核对，据此追踪「筹资活动产生的负债的现金变动」。

examples.en: The schedule compared cash changes in financing liabilities with the related financing flows reported for the period.
examples.zh: 附表比较了「筹资活动产生的负债的现金变动」与本期报告的相关筹资现金流。

collocations: identify cash changes in financing liabilities
reconcile cash changes in financing liabilities
disclose cash changes in financing liabilities

words.enDefinition: cash received from customers who initially bought goods or services on credit

examples.en: The retailer compared cash collected from credit customers with the total amount invoiced during the same quarter.
examples.zh: 零售商把「收回的赊销货款」与同季度的开票总额进行了比较。

examples.en: Our worksheet used credit sales and receivables balances to calculate cash collected from credit customers.
examples.zh: 练习表用赊销收入和应收账款余额计算「收回的赊销货款」。

collocations: calculate cash collected from credit customers
track cash collected from credit customers
reconcile cash collected from credit customers

words.enDefinition: the delay between recording a sale and receiving the cash

examples.en: The sample report showed a longer cash collection lag after customers received extended payment terms.
examples.zh: 客户获得更长付款期后，样本报告显示「现金回收时滞」拉长了。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how the cash collection lag explained differences between revenue and receipts.
examples.zh: 导师问，「现金回收时滞」可以怎样解释收入和收款的差异。

words.enDefinition: A budget schedule showing when cash from sales or other receivables is expected to be collected.

examples.en: The cash collections schedule showed that some June sales would only be collected in July.
examples.zh: 「预计现金收款明细表」显示，六月的部分销售款要到七月才收得到。

examples.en: We used the cash collections schedule to estimate how much money was available for the workshop.
examples.zh: 我们用「预计现金收款明细表」估算有多少资金可以给工场使用。

words.enDefinition: the portion of earnings reflected in cash flow

examples.en: The exercise separated the cash component of profit from the portion driven by accruals.
examples.zh: 练习把盈利的「现金流部分」和由应计项目形成的部分分开。

examples.en: We compared the cash component across two years after checking which cash measure the worksheet used.
examples.zh: 我们核对了练习表采用的现金指标，再比较两年的「现金流部分」。

collocations: estimate the cash component of earnings
compare the cash component across years

words.enDefinition: inventory days plus receivables days minus payables days

examples.en: The exercise showed a shorter cash conversion cycle after customers paid sooner in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中顾客更早付款后，练习表显示「现金转换周期」缩短了。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why paying suppliers later could shorten the cash conversion cycle.
examples.zh: 导师问，为什么晚一些支付供应商款项可能缩短「现金转换周期」。

words.enDefinition: cash and cash equivalent balances leaving the reporting group when it disposes of a business

examples.en: We deducted cash disposed of from the consideration received to calculate the example's net investing cash inflow.
examples.zh: 我们从收到的对价中扣除「随业务转出的现金」，计算案例的投资现金净流入。

examples.en: The note disclosed cash disposed of along with the total consideration received when the subsidiary was sold.
examples.zh: 附注披露了「随业务转出的现金」，以及出售子公司收到的对价总额。

collocations: report the amount of cash disposed of

words.zhGloss: 现金等价物的到期标准
words.enDefinition: the short period to maturity considered when assessing whether an investment qualifies as a cash equivalent
acceptedZhAnswers: 现金等价物的到期标准

examples.en: The class discussed the cash equivalent maturity criterion and measured the term from the date of acquisition.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论了「现金等价物的到期标准」，从取得日算起衡量期限。

examples.en: The example applied the cash equivalent maturity criterion alongside the conditions on liquidity and risk of value changes.
examples.zh: 示例把「现金等价物的到期标准」与流动性和价值变动风险的条件结合起来应用。

collocations: assess the cash equivalent maturity criterion
apply the cash equivalent maturity criterion
meet the cash equivalent maturity criterion

words.enDefinition: assigning actual cash flows to categories such as operating, investing and financing

examples.en: We discussed cash flow classification after finding two parts to the company's loan payment.
examples.zh: 发现这家公司的贷款支付包含两部分后，我们讨论了「现金流量分类」。

examples.en: The workshop used cash flow classification to show where payments for new equipment would appear.
examples.zh: 工作坊通过「现金流量分类」说明购入新设备的付款会列在哪里。

words.expression: cash flow from a hedged item
words.lemma: cash flow from a hedged item
words.zhGloss: 被套期项目产生的现金流
words.enDefinition: a cash inflow or outflow from an item or transaction exposed to a risk that a hedge aims to offset
acceptedZhAnswers: 被套期项目产生的现金流
acceptedEnVariants: cash flow from a hedged item

examples.en: We first identified the cash flow from a hedged item using the original sale invoice in the example.
examples.zh: 我们先用示例的原销售发票确定了「被套期项目产生的现金流」。

examples.en: The tutor showed where the cash flow from a hedged item appeared before discussing the related derivative contract.
examples.zh: 导师先演示了「被套期项目产生的现金流」列在哪里，再讨论相关衍生品合约。

collocations: classify the cash flow from a hedged item
identify the cash flow from a hedged item
report the cash flow from a hedged item

words.expression: cash flow from acquiring non-controlling interests
words.lemma: cash flow from acquiring non-controlling interests
words.zhGloss: 收购非控股权益产生的现金流
words.enDefinition: cash paid to buy an additional interest in a subsidiary that the reporting parent already controls
acceptedZhAnswers: 收购非控股权益产生的现金流
acceptedEnVariants: cash flow from acquiring non-controlling interests
cash flow from acquiring noncontrolling interests

examples.en: The IFRS example classified cash flow from acquiring non-controlling interests as financing because the parent retained control.
examples.zh: IFRS 示例把「收购非控股权益产生的现金流」列作筹资现金流，因为母公司仍保有控制权。

examples.en: We traced the cash flow from acquiring non-controlling interests to a purchase from minority shareholders in June.
examples.zh: 我们将「收购非控股权益产生的现金流」追溯到六月从少数股东购入股份的交易。

collocations: report cash flow from acquiring non-controlling interests
disclose cash flow from acquiring non-controlling interests
identify cash flow from acquiring non-controlling interests

words.enDefinition: a separately presented amount or category within a statement of cash flows

examples.en: The tutor asked which cash flow line item would include the proceeds from selling a printer.
examples.zh: 导师问，出售打印机所得会列入「现金流量表具体项目」中的哪一项。

examples.en: We traced a cash flow line item to the equipment note in the fictional report.
examples.zh: 我们把一个「现金流量表具体项目」追溯到虚构报告的设备附注。

collocations: identify a cash flow line item
report a cash flow line item separately

words.enDefinition: the usefulness of reported cash flows for assessing recurring cash generation

examples.en: The case examined cash flow quality after a large payment arrived unusually early that quarter.
examples.zh: 一笔大额款项在该季度异常提前到账，案例以此考察「现金流质量」。

examples.en: Our group compared cash flow quality after accounting for the effect of the fictional asset sale.
examples.zh: 小组在考虑虚构资产出售的影响后，对「现金流质量」作了比较。

words.enDefinition: an intermediate sum for a selected group of cash flow amounts, such as a major activity category

examples.en: The class recalculated the cash flow subtotal before looking at the final movement in cash.
examples.zh: 课堂先重算了「现金流量小计」，然后才看现金最终变动。

examples.en: The report placed a cash flow subtotal at the end of each activity section.
examples.zh: 报告在每类活动结束处列出一处「现金流量小计」。

words.enDefinition: the likelihood that a business can keep generating its cash flows

examples.en: We discussed cash flow sustainability after excluding proceeds from the fictional company's property sale.
examples.zh: 剔除虚构公司出售房产的所得后，我们讨论了「现金流可持续性」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which recurring activities mattered most for cash flow sustainability in the sample.
examples.zh: 导师问，样本中的哪些经常性活动对「现金流可持续性」最重要。

words.enDefinition: when actual cash receipts or payments take place

examples.en: The case traced cash flow timing to explain why two months showed similar sales but different collections.
examples.zh: 案例追踪「现金流发生时点」，解释为什么两个月销售额相近而收款额不同。

examples.en: We distinguished cash flow timing from the overall amount collected during the full classroom period.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「现金流发生时点」与课堂所讨论整个期间的收款总额。

collocations: a change in cash flow timing

words.expression: cash flow to net income ratio
words.lemma: cash flow to net income ratio
words.zhGloss: 经营现金流与净利润之比
words.enDefinition: operating cash flow divided by net income for the same period
acceptedZhAnswers: 经营现金流与净利润之比
acceptedEnVariants: cash flow to net income ratio

words.enDefinition: cash receipts and payments associated with taking out and repaying borrowings, presented according to the applicable categories

a constructive obligation arising from past practice

words.enDefinition: Under IAS 37, a possible asset from past events whose existence depends on uncertain events outside full entity control.

examples.en: The exercise classified the possible compensation as a contingent asset while the claim's outcome remained uncertain.
examples.zh: 索赔结果尚未确定时，练习将可能获得的赔偿归为「或有资产」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked what would happen to the contingent asset if the receipt became virtually certain.
examples.zh: 老师问，如果收到款项基本确定，这项「或有资产」会怎样处理。

words.enDefinition: Under IAS 37, a possible obligation or a present obligation not recognised because outflow is not probable or measurement unreliable.

examples.en: The note described a contingent liability because it was unclear whether the company would have to pay.
examples.zh: 由于公司是否必须付款尚不清楚，附注说明了一项「或有负债」。

examples.en: The class distinguished a contingent liability in the notes from a provision on the balance sheet.
examples.zh: 同学们区分了附注中的「或有负债」和资产负债表中的预计负债。

collocations: describe the nature of a contingent liability

words.enDefinition: A conditional right to consideration for goods or services already transferred, with a condition beyond the passage of time.

examples.en: The case recorded a contract asset because payment for completed work depended on delivering the final component.
examples.zh: 已完成工作的付款还取决于最后一个部件的交付，因此例题确认了「合同资产」。

examples.en: We explained why the contract asset became a receivable only after the remaining delivery condition was satisfied.
examples.zh: 我们解释了为什么只有满足剩下的交付条件后，「合同资产」才转为应收款。

collocations: reclassify a contract asset as a receivable
disclose the opening contract asset balance

words.enDefinition: In IFRS 15 disclosure, balances of receivables, contract assets and contract liabilities arising from customer contracts.

examples.en: The note compared contract balances at the beginning and end of the year for the service contracts.
examples.zh: 附注比较了服务合同的年初和年末「合同相关余额」。

examples.en: Our class checked the contract balances before explaining why the company had received more cash than reported revenue.
examples.zh: 在解释公司收到的现金为何超过列报收入前，同学们先核对了「合同相关余额」。

collocations: reconcile opening and closing contract balances

words.enDefinition: An obligation to transfer goods or services for consideration received or due from the customer.

examples.en: The company recorded a contract liability when it took advance payment for a course starting in June.
examples.zh: 公司收取六月开课的课程预付款时确认了「合同负债」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which service would have to be delivered before the contract liability could decrease.
examples.zh: 老师问，交付哪项服务后「合同负债」才能减少。

collocations: recognise revenue from a contract liability

words.expression: contribution per unit of limiting factor
words.lemma: contribution per unit of limiting factor
words.zhGloss: 单位限制资源的边际贡献
words.enDefinition: Contribution margin earned for each unit of a constrained resource used
acceptedZhAnswers: 单位限制资源的边际贡献
acceptedEnVariants: contribution per unit of limiting factor

examples.en: The worksheet ranked products by contribution per unit of limiting factor when labour hours were scarce.
examples.zh: 工时紧张时，练习表按「单位限制资源的边际贡献」给产品排序。

examples.en: We recalculated contribution per unit of limiting factor after the machine time per piece changed.
examples.zh: 单件占用的机器时间变化后，我们重新计算了「单位限制资源的边际贡献」。

collocations: calculate contribution per unit of limiting factor
rank by contribution per unit of limiting factor
compare contribution per unit of limiting factor

words.enDefinition: The principle that a manager's performance should be assessed on factors they can substantially influence.

examples.en: The controllability principle led our tutor to exclude building rent when assessing the workshop supervisor's performance.
examples.zh: 按「可控性原则」，老师评估工场负责人的表现时剔除了房租。

examples.en: The class discussed how the controllability principle applied when a supplier changed prices across the organisation.
examples.zh: 全班讨论了供应商面向整个机构调价时，怎样应用「可控性原则」。

collocations: use the controllability principle in performance evaluation

words.enDefinition: Capital or assets whose use a divisional manager can influence

examples.en: The worksheet excluded head office equipment from the manager's controllable investment.
examples.zh: 练习表把总部设备排除在经理的「可控投资额」之外。

examples.en: The tutor asked which assets belonged in controllable investment for this division.
examples.zh: 导师问，该分部的哪些资产应计入「可控投资额」？

words.enDefinition: A measure of divisional profit based on revenue and costs that the division manager can influence.

examples.en: The class calculated controllable profit before adding charges that the print room manager had no authority over.
examples.zh: 全班先算「可控利润」，然后再纳入印刷室经理无权决定的收费项目。

examples.en: The case used controllable profit to review the manager's decisions about prices, staffing and local supplies.
examples.zh: 案例用「可控利润」评估经理在定价、人员和当地物资采购方面的决策。

collocations: evaluate a manager using controllable profit
compare controllable profit with traceable profit

words.enDefinition: Controllable profit after a charge on capital the manager controls

examples.en: The controllable residual income calculation excluded equipment controlled by the central office.
examples.zh: 计算「可控剩余收益」时，排除了由总部控制的设备。

examples.en: We compared controllable residual income with the result for all capital used by the division.
examples.zh: 我们把「可控剩余收益」与计入分部全部占用资本后的结果作了对照。

words.enDefinition: the direct labour and manufacturing overhead costs of turning materials into finished output

examples.en: The tutor assigned conversion costs separately from the paper and covers used for the notebooks.
examples.zh: 导师把「加工成本」和笔记本所用的纸张、封面成本分开分配。

examples.en: We calculated the conversion costs for the finishing department using labour and applied overhead together.
examples.zh: 我们用人工和已分配间接费用合计计算了后道加工部门的「加工成本」。

words.enDefinition: excess reserves later released to make earnings look better

examples.en: The class discussed cookie jar reserves after the fictional report showed unusually large reversals.
examples.zh: 虚构报告显示异常大额的转回后，同学们讨论了「用于调节盈利的储备」。

examples.en: Our tutor noted that a steady profit series alone did not establish cookie jar reserves.
examples.zh: 导师指出，仅有平稳的利润数据不足以确认存在「用于调节盈利的储备」。

collocations: the release of cookie jar reserves

words.enDefinition: the process of collecting costs for later assignment to jobs, departments, activities or other objects

examples.en: During cost accumulation, we grouped the printer charges with other costs for the same job.
examples.zh: 进行「成本归集」时，我们把打印机费用和同一作业的其他成本归在一起。

examples.en: The lecturer demonstrated cost accumulation for two production departments before discussing overhead allocation in class.
examples.zh: 讲师先演示了两个生产部门怎么进行「成本归集」，然后讨论间接费用分配。

words.enDefinition: an explanation of why particular allocation bases or methods were chosen for an indirect cost

examples.en: The cost allocation rationale explained why we used floor space to distribute the shared workshop rent.
examples.zh: 「成本分配依据」说明了为什么用占用面积分摊共用工作室的租金。

examples.en: Our tutor asked for a clearer cost allocation rationale after seeing that the two departments used equipment differently.
examples.zh: 导师看到两个部门使用设备的方式不同，要求写清「成本分配依据」。

words.enDefinition: identifying the objects that should bear costs and assigning the costs to them by tracing or allocation

examples.en: The worksheet covered cost assignment after we had collected the costs for both printing orders.
examples.zh: 我们归集了两笔印刷订单的成本后，练习表接着讲「成本归属分配」。

examples.en: A new cost assignment method charged the exhibition's equipment use to the groups that used it.
examples.zh: 新的「成本归属分配」方法把展览的设备使用成本记给用过设备的各组。

words.enDefinition: systematically undercosting some items and overcosting others because of how shared costs are assigned

examples.en: The lecturer used cost cross-subsidisation to explain how custom orders appeared cheaper than they really were.
examples.zh: 讲师用「产品间成本交叉补贴」解释，为什么定制订单看起来比实际便宜。

examples.en: The broader allocation base caused cost cross-subsidisation between standard products and the smaller specialist lines.
examples.zh: 粗放的分配基础让标准产品与量较小的专门产品之间出现了「成本交叉补贴」。

words.enDefinition: a misleading assignment of costs that results in inaccurate cost estimates for products, services or other objects

examples.en: The simple allocation method caused cost distortion because two products used very different setup times.
examples.zh: 两种产品所需准备时间差别很大，简单分配法造成了「成本扭曲」。

examples.en: We looked for cost distortion after seeing two identical overhead charges for very different orders.
examples.zh: 发现两笔差异很大的订单间接费用竟然一样后，我们检查是否有「成本扭曲」。

words.enDefinition: the process of choosing a measure that reasonably reflects what causes a particular cost to change

examples.en: The tutor treated cost-driver selection as a separate step before we calculated any allocation rates.
examples.zh: 导师把「成本动因选择」列为一个单独步骤，完成后才算各项分配率。

examples.en: We revisited cost-driver selection when the number of orders no longer reflected the inspection work needed.
examples.zh: 订单数不再能反映必要的检查工作量时，我们重新作了「成本动因选择」。

words.enDefinition: a classification of costs according to the level of activity that causes them

examples.en: The cost hierarchy placed setup costs at the batch level and assembly costs at the unit level.
examples.zh: 「成本层级」把准备成本列为批次级，把组装成本列为单位级。

examples.en: Our tutor used a cost hierarchy to explain why not all costs followed the number of units.
examples.zh: 导师用「成本层级」说明，为什么并非所有成本都随产量变动。

collocations: classify activities in a cost hierarchy

words.enDefinition: The activity level at which two alternatives have equal total cost

examples.en: The cost indifference point occurred where the two cost lines crossed on the graph.
examples.zh: 图上两条成本线交叉的位置就是「成本无差别点」。

examples.en: We reported the cost indifference point as the number of units made each month.
examples.zh: 我们用月产量件数表示「成本无差别点」。

collocations: production below the cost indifference point

words.enDefinition: anything for which a separate cost is measured, such as a product, job, service or department

examples.en: We treated each custom sign as a cost object because it used different materials and time.
examples.zh: 由于每块定制标牌的用料和工时各异，我们把每块都当作「成本对象」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to identify the cost object before classifying any of the listed expenses.
examples.zh: 导师让我们先确定「成本对象」，再对列出的各项开支分类。

collocations: trace costs to a cost object
allocate overhead to a cost object

words.enDefinition: the total production cost of goods completed during an accounting period

examples.en: The class calculated cost of goods manufactured before using finished goods balances to calculate cost of goods sold.
examples.zh: 全班先计算「完工产品成本」，再用产成品余额计算销售成本。

examples.en: We included the opening unfinished work when calculating cost of goods manufactured for the example month.
examples.zh: 计算示例月份的「完工产品成本」时，我们纳入了期初在产品。

collocations: schedule of cost of goods manufactured

words.enDefinition: An amount by which the actual cost of an activity or project exceeds the planned or estimated cost.

examples.en: A cost overrun appeared in the final repair worksheet when the practice workshop added a second inspection.
examples.zh: 模拟工场增加了第二次检查之后，最终维修练习表出现了「成本超支」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the cost overrun had come from higher prices or a larger order.
examples.zh: 老师问，「成本超支」是由于价格更高，还是因为订单量更大。

collocations: a cost overrun on a project

words.enDefinition: the amount of a cost category divided by the equivalent units assigned to that category

examples.en: We found the cost per equivalent unit for conversion before assigning any costs to unfinished output.
examples.zh: 给未完工产量分配成本之前，我们先求出了加工的「单位约当成本」。

examples.en: The lecturer compared cost per equivalent unit for materials with the amount calculated for conversion.
examples.zh: 讲师把材料的「单位约当成本」与加工部分算出的数字作了比较。

collocations: estimate the cost per equivalent unit
cost per equivalent unit for conversion

words.zhGloss: 单位瓶颈工时工厂成本
words.enDefinition: Total factory operating costs divided by available hours at the bottleneck
acceptedZhAnswers: 单位瓶颈工时工厂成本

examples.en: The worksheet used total factory operating expense to calculate cost per factory hour in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习表用工厂运营支出总额，计算「单位瓶颈工时工厂成本」。

examples.en: Extra time at the bottleneck changed cost per factory hour in the workshop example.
examples.zh: 工作坊示例中，瓶颈工序增加的时间改变了「单位瓶颈工时工厂成本」。

collocations: compare returns with cost per factory hour

words.enDefinition: An internal charge calculated by adding a margin to defined cost

examples.en: The worksheet calculated a cost-plus transfer price using the factory's standard cost and markup.
examples.zh: 练习表按照工厂的标准成本和加成数额，计算了「成本加成内部转移价」。

examples.en: The two divisions compared their profit under a cost-plus transfer price in class.
examples.zh: 两家分部在课堂案例里对照了采用「成本加成内部转移价」时各自的利润。

collocations: choose a markup for a cost-plus transfer price

words.enDefinition: a check that costs collected in a pool agree with source records and assigned or remaining balances

examples.en: Our cost pool reconciliation found a printing charge that had been included twice in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们的「成本库核对」发现，有一笔印刷费用在工作表里计了两次。

examples.en: The lecturer requested a cost pool reconciliation before comparing the amounts allocated to each product.
examples.zh: 讲师要求先做「成本库核对」，再比较分配给各项产品的金额。

words.enDefinition: a schedule showing where the costs to be accounted for have been assigned
