collocations: an investing cash inflow from equipment sales

words.enDefinition: cash paid in connection with investing activities, such as buying long-term assets

examples.en: The purchase of the new printer appeared as an investing cash outflow on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 购置新打印机的付款在练习表上列为「投资现金流出」。

examples.en: Our group classified the equipment deposit as an investing cash outflow in the classroom case.
examples.zh: 我们组把课堂案例的设备订金列为「投资现金流出」。

collocations: an investing cash outflow from asset purchases

words.enDefinition: A responsibility centre whose manager is accountable for profit and the capital invested in the unit.

examples.en: The workshop was an investment centre because its manager oversaw profits and could approve equipment purchases.
examples.zh: 工场经理负责利润，也有权批准设备采购，因此工场是「投资中心」。

examples.en: We compared the profit and invested capital of each investment centre in the final classroom report.
examples.zh: 在课堂最后的报告中，我们比较了各「投资中心」的利润和投入资本。

collocations: the assets of an investment centre

words.enDefinition: A cost that does not change between the options being considered

examples.en: We treated unchanged insurance as an irrelevant cost in the weekend opening decision.
examples.zh: 在决定周末是否营业时，我们把金额不变的保险费视为「非相关成本」。

examples.en: The tutor asked why the old equipment price was an irrelevant cost.
examples.zh: 导师问，为什么旧设备的购入价属于「非相关成本」？

collocations: omit an irrelevant cost from a comparison
treat a cost as an irrelevant cost

words.enDefinition: a record showing direct materials, direct labour and allocated overhead for a specific job

examples.en: The job cost sheet listed the paper used for the drama society's poster order.
examples.zh: 「作业成本单」列了话剧社海报订单所用的纸张。

examples.en: I checked the job cost sheet before comparing the budget with the cost of the finished display.
examples.zh: 我先查了「作业成本单」，再比较预算和展示台实际完工的成本。

collocations: post costs to a job cost sheet

words.enDefinition: a ledger containing the detailed cost records for individual jobs

examples.en: The job ledger showed which completed orders still needed their labour costs to be entered.
examples.zh: 「作业成本明细账」显示了哪些已完工订单还需要录入人工成本。

examples.en: We used the job ledger to trace the cost of plywood back to the theatre display.
examples.zh: 我们通过「作业成本明细账」把胶合板成本追溯到了剧场展示台。

collocations: post costs to the job ledger

words.enDefinition: a reference number used to identify a specific order or work assignment in a costing or tracking system

examples.en: We wrote the job number on each receipt before entering its cost on the sheet.
examples.zh: 填成本单之前，我们在每张收据上写了「作业编号」。

examples.en: The supervisor asked me to check the job number before assigning the materials to the order.
examples.zh: 主管请我先核对「作业编号」，再把材料成本记到订单上。

collocations: match a receipt to a job number

words.enDefinition: a system that accumulates and assigns costs to individual orders, jobs or batches

examples.en: The print shop used job order costing because each society requested a different set of materials.
examples.zh: 各社团要求的材料各不相同，印刷店采用「分批成本法」。

examples.en: Our lecturer used job order costing to estimate what the custom display had cost to make.
examples.zh: 讲师用「分批成本法」估算制作定制展示台花了多少钱。

words.enDefinition: the process of apportioning costs incurred before the split-off point among outputs of a joint production process

examples.en: Our example used joint cost allocation to assign the shared dairy processing costs to both outputs.
examples.zh: 示例使用「联合成本分配」把乳品共同加工成本分配给两种产出。

examples.en: We compared how two methods of joint cost allocation affected the reported cost of each product.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两种「联合成本分配」方法如何影响各产品的报告成本。

collocations: apply a joint cost allocation method
compare bases for joint cost allocation
calculate the result of joint cost allocation

words.enDefinition: one of multiple significant products obtained together from a single process

examples.en: The tutor treated the two saleable paper grades as joint products from one processing line.
examples.zh: 导师把一条加工线产出的两种可售纸张等级视为「联产品」。

examples.en: Each joint product had a substantial sales value in the example, unlike the leftover scraps.
examples.zh: 示例中每种「联产品」都有可观的销售价值，剩下的碎料则不同。

words.enDefinition: a process that produces two or more outputs together before each can be identified separately

examples.en: The lecturer used joint production to describe how one cutting process yielded two usable materials.
examples.zh: 讲师用「联合生产」描述一个切割过程如何同时产出两种可用材料。

examples.en: We discussed whether the costs of joint production could be traced to each separate output.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「联合生产」的成本是否能追溯到每种独立产出。

words.enDefinition: Choosing whether to continue or discontinue an existing line or segment

examples.en: The keep-or-drop decision compared the contribution lost with the costs that would disappear.
examples.zh: 「保留或停办决策」比较了放弃的边际贡献与能节省的成本。

examples.en: Our tutor used a keep-or-drop decision involving a campus stall with falling sales.
examples.zh: 导师用一项销量下滑的校园摊位业务介绍了「保留或停办决策」。

collocations: a keep-or-drop decision for a product line

words.enDefinition: Benefits provided in exchange for the services of people who direct and control the entity's activities.

examples.en: The sample note broke down key management compensation into salary, pension benefits and share-based payments.
examples.zh: 示例附注把「关键管理人员薪酬」分成工资、养老金福利和股份支付。

examples.en: Our group compared the categories in the key management compensation note with those in the prior-year report.
examples.zh: 我们组把「关键管理人员薪酬」附注的类别与上年报告中的类别作了对比。

collocations: review the note on key management compensation

words.enDefinition: People with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling an entity's activities, directly or indirectly.

examples.en: The class identified key management personnel based on who actually directed the group's activities in the case.
examples.zh: 同学们依据例题中谁实际领导集团经营活动来识别「关键管理人员」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why the note on key management personnel included directors from outside the executive team.
examples.zh: 老师问，「关键管理人员」附注为什么纳入了行政团队以外的董事。

collocations: disclose remuneration of key management personnel

words.enDefinition: The cost effect of using more or fewer labour hours than the standard allows for actual output, valued at the standard labour rate.

examples.en: The faster assembly jig gave the team a favourable labour efficiency variance at the standard hourly rate.
examples.zh: 按标准小时费率计，更快的装配夹具让团队出现了有利的「人工效率差异」。

examples.en: Our lecturer separated the labour efficiency variance from time spent waiting for a replacement tool.
examples.zh: 老师把「人工效率差异」与等待替换工具花掉的时间分开分析。

collocations: analyse the labour efficiency variance separately from idle time

words.enDefinition: A limit on available staff time for carrying out planned work

examples.en: The case added a labour-hour constraint after the weekday shifts were reduced.
examples.zh: 工作日班次减少后，案例加入了「人工工时约束」。

examples.en: We compared three production plans under the same labour-hour constraint in class.
examples.zh: 全班在相同「人工工时约束」下比较了三种生产计划。

words.enDefinition: The difference between the actual and standard labour rates multiplied by the relevant actual labour hours.

examples.en: The labour rate variance was adverse after an experienced technician took over the evening repair shift.
examples.zh: 一名经验丰富的技工接手晚间维修班次后，出现了不利的「人工费率差异」。

examples.en: The labour rate variance was zero because everyone was paid at the standard rate for the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中所有人都按标准费率领薪，因此「人工费率差异」为零。

collocations: explain an adverse labour rate variance
separate the labour rate variance from efficiency

words.enDefinition: Moving existing employees to work on other tasks or activities

examples.en: The costing case included labour redeployment after the first production line closed.
examples.zh: 第一条生产线关闭后，成本案例考虑了「人员调配」。

examples.en: Our group assessed labour redeployment before estimating any reduction in payroll spending.
examples.zh: 我们组先研究了「人员调配」，再估算薪资支出能减少多少。

words.enDefinition: a document recording time spent on particular jobs or activities by a worker

examples.en: The labour time record showed how much of the afternoon was spent assembling the display stand.
examples.zh: 「人工用时记录」写明了下午有多少时间花在组装展示架上。

examples.en: We checked the labour time record before charging the work to the two orders.
examples.zh: 把人工费用计入两笔订单前，我们核对了「人工用时记录」。

collocations: hours on a labour time record

words.enDefinition: The tendency for the time or effort per unit to fall as people gain experience with repeat work.

examples.en: The worksheet showed a learning curve effect as the same team grew faster at assembling each successive batch.
examples.zh: 练习表呈现了「学习曲线效应」，同一个小组装配下一批产品时越来越快。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the learning curve effect would still matter for a one-off printing job.
examples.zh: 老师问，对于只做一次的印刷工作，「学习曲线效应」是否仍然重要。

collocations: allow for the learning curve effect
incorporate the learning curve effect into labour standards

words.zhGloss: 偿还租赁负债本金的款项
words.enDefinition: the principal portions of lease payments that reduce the carrying amount of a lessee's lease liability
acceptedZhAnswers: 偿还租赁负债本金的款项

examples.en: Our IFRS example placed lease principal payments in financing cash flows and showed the interest component separately.
examples.zh: 我们的 IFRS 示例把「偿还租赁负债本金的款项」列作筹资现金流，另行列示利息部分。

examples.en: We compared lease principal payments with the total cash paid under the same lease during the year.
examples.zh: 我们把「偿还租赁负债本金的款项」与同一租约当年的现金付款总额作了比较。

collocations: separate lease principal payments from interest

words.zhGloss: 由法律或合同产生的义务
words.enDefinition: Under IAS 37, an obligation arising from a contract, legislation, or another operation of law.
acceptedZhAnswers: 由法律或合同产生的义务

examples.en: The case described a legal obligation to restore the leased site under the terms of its contract.
examples.zh: 例题说明，按租赁合同条款，恢复租赁场地属于一项「由法律或合同产生的义务」。

examples.en: Our tutor distinguished a legal obligation from a promise created by a company's established business practices.
examples.zh: 老师区分了「由法律或合同产生的义务」和根据公司一贯经营做法形成的承诺。

collocations: a legal obligation under a contract

words.enDefinition: Unadjusted quoted prices in accessible active markets for identical assets or liabilities at the measurement date.

examples.en: The report used level 1 inputs for shares with current quoted prices in an accessible active market.
examples.zh: 报告对在可进入的活跃市场有当前报价的股票采用「第一层次输入值」。

examples.en: The exercise excluded adjusted quotes for similar items from the list of level 1 inputs.
examples.zh: 练习列举「第一层次输入值」时，没有纳入类似项目经调整的报价。

words.enDefinition: Observable inputs other than Level 1 quoted prices, obtained directly or indirectly for an asset or liability.

examples.en: The valuation used level 2 inputs from observable yield curves for the remaining term of the instrument.
examples.zh: 估值采用可观察收益率曲线中对应工具剩余期限的「第二层次输入值」。

examples.en: The case treated quoted prices for similar assets in active markets as level 2 inputs.
examples.zh: 例题将类似资产在活跃市场的报价列作「第二层次输入值」。

collocations: observable yield curves as level 2 inputs

words.enDefinition: Unobservable variables used to measure fair value when relevant observable market inputs are unavailable.

examples.en: The valuation used level 3 inputs for rental growth because relevant market data was unavailable.
examples.zh: 缺少相关市场数据，因此这项估值对租金增长采用了「第三层次输入值」。

examples.en: The tutor asked how the note explained the level 3 inputs used to value the property.
examples.zh: 老师问，附注怎样解释物业估值采用的「第三层次输入值」。

collocations: estimate fair value with level 3 inputs

words.enDefinition: A rollforward explaining changes between opening and closing balances for recurring Level 3 fair value measurements.

examples.en: The level 3 reconciliation showed a gain as well as assets sold during the reporting period.
examples.zh: 「第三层次余额调节表」同时列示了一笔利得和报告期内售出的资产。

examples.en: We used the level 3 reconciliation to trace how the closing fair value differed from the opening balance.
examples.zh: 我们用「第三层次余额调节表」追踪期末公允价值与期初余额为何不同。

collocations: show transfers in a level 3 reconciliation

words.enDefinition: sales measured across comparable operations under defined inclusion rules

examples.en: The report defined like-for-like sales using stores that were open in both periods under review.
examples.zh: 报告用两个比较期间都在营业的门店来界定「可比口径销售额」。

examples.en: Our group checked whether online orders were included in like-for-like sales for the sample retailer.
examples.zh: 小组核对了样本零售商的「可比口径销售额」是否包含网上订单。

words.enDefinition: comparing uses of a single scarce resource, commonly by ranking products by contribution per unit of that resource

examples.en: We used limiting factor analysis when the workshop had fewer labour hours than planned.
examples.zh: 工作室可用工时比计划少时，我们用了「限制因素分析」。

examples.en: The limiting factor analysis compared both products using minutes on the same machine.
examples.zh: 「限制因素分析」按两种产品占用同一台机器的分钟数作了比较。

words.enDefinition: How individual items are shown on separate lines in a financial statement.

examples.en: The tutor reviewed line item presentation after the sample statement added a separate line for financing expenses.
examples.zh: 示例报表新增一行单独列示融资费用后，老师核查了「报表项目列示」。

examples.en: Our group changed the line item presentation so the major expense categories were easier to find.
examples.zh: 我们组调整了「报表项目列示」，让主要费用类别更容易找到。

words.enDefinition: cash and available funding above the amount needed for foreseeable obligations

examples.en: The sample report showed how much liquidity headroom remained after allowing for its scheduled bills.
examples.zh: 样本报告显示，在计入预计付款后还剩多少「流动性余量」。

examples.en: We compared liquidity headroom across two seasons because the fictional company's payment schedule changed.
examples.zh: 由于虚构公司的付款时间表会变化，我们比较了两个季节的「流动性余量」。

words.enDefinition: a significant exposure to difficulty meeting payments that is concentrated in a common counterparty or other shared source

examples.en: Depending on one finance provider created a liquidity risk concentration in the example used during our course.
examples.zh: 在课堂示例中，依赖单一融资方造成了「流动性风险集中」。

examples.en: The note on liquidity risk concentration explained how much of the company's supplier financing involved one bank.
examples.zh: 「流动性风险集中」附注说明了公司有多少供应商融资涉及同一家银行。

words.enDefinition: an agreement by which parties resolve a lawsuit

examples.en: The sample report explained that a litigation settlement affected the fictional company's annual expenses.
examples.zh: 样本报告解释，一项「诉讼和解」影响了虚构公司的年度费用。

examples.en: Our group checked where the litigation settlement appeared in the reconciliation of adjusted net income.
examples.zh: 我们小组核对了「诉讼和解」出现在调整后净利润调节表的哪里。

collocations: costs associated with a litigation settlement

words.enDefinition: A part of an organisation showing a loss under the measure used

examples.en: The loss-making segment showed a positive contribution before the central costs were allocated.
examples.zh: 在分摊总部成本之前，这个「亏损分部」仍有正的边际贡献。

examples.en: Our group checked which expenses would actually disappear with a loss-making segment.
examples.zh: 我们组核对了一个「亏损分部」停办后，哪些支出才会消失。

words.expression: loss of control of a subsidiary
words.lemma: loss of control of a subsidiary
words.enDefinition: an event after which an entity no longer controls a company that it previously consolidated
acceptedEnVariants: loss of control of a subsidiary

examples.en: The group reported the loss of control of a subsidiary after selling its entire stake to another buyer.
examples.zh: 集团把全部持股卖给另一买方后，报告了「丧失对子公司的控制」。

examples.en: Our case separated cash flows from the loss of control of a subsidiary in the investing section.
examples.zh: 案例在投资部分单列了「丧失对子公司的控制」产生的现金流。

collocations: account for the loss of control of a subsidiary
report the loss of control of a subsidiary
disclose the loss of control of a subsidiary

words.enDefinition: payments under leases of assets that qualify as low value under the relevant reporting rules

examples.en: The accounting note disclosed low-value lease payments for several small office devices used by the company.
examples.zh: 会计附注披露了公司使用的几台小型办公设备所涉及的「低价值资产租赁付款」。

examples.en: We found low-value lease payments in the operating section because the IFRS example applied the recognition exemption.
examples.zh: 我们在经营部分找到了「低价值资产租赁付款」，因为 IFRS 示例采用了确认豁免。

words.enDefinition: assigning costs in proportion to the machine time recorded for each product, job or department

examples.en: We used machine-hour allocation because the larger signs needed significantly more time on the printer.
examples.zh: 印大标牌占用设备的时间长得多，所以我们用了「按机器工时分配」。

examples.en: The lecturer compared machine-hour allocation with allocation based on the number of posters in each order.
examples.zh: 讲师把「按机器工时分配」和按各单海报数量分配作了比较。

words.enDefinition: an overhead or cost rate calculated per hour of machine use

examples.en: We used the machine-hour rate to calculate how much overhead to assign to each order.
examples.zh: 我们用「每机器工时费率」计算各笔订单该分到多少间接费用。

examples.en: The machine-hour rate rose when we forecast the same overhead across fewer hours of use.
examples.zh: 预计把同样的间接费用分摊到更少的使用时数后，「每机器工时费率」提高了。

words.enDefinition: the amount of time machines are operated, often used as a measure for assigning costs

examples.en: The workshop allocated equipment costs using machine hours recorded by the cutting department each week.
examples.zh: 工作室用切割部门每周记录的「机器工时」分配设备成本。

examples.en: I included all the machine hours the equipment spent printing the two exhibition banners.
examples.zh: 我把设备印两幅展览横幅所用的全部「机器工时」都计了进去。

words.enDefinition: An approach in which managers focus on significant departures from plans or expected limits.

examples.en: Management by exception kept the class discussion focused on unexpected labour costs and the unusually low sales.
examples.zh: 「例外管理」让课堂讨论集中在意外的人工成本以及异常偏低的销量上。

examples.en: In the exercise, management by exception meant checking flagged figures before reviewing small routine differences.
examples.zh: 在练习中，「例外管理」意味着先查被标记的数字，再看例行的小额差异。

collocations: apply management by exception to budget review
an example of management by exception

words.zhGloss: 管理层定义的业绩指标
words.enDefinition: under IFRS 18, an income-and-expense subtotal used in public communications to convey management's view of company-wide performance, excluding subtotals specified by IFRS
acceptedZhAnswers: 管理层定义的业绩指标

examples.en: The sample IFRS note reconciled a management-defined performance measure to the closest specified profit subtotal.
examples.zh: 样本 IFRS 附注将「管理层定义的业绩指标」调节至最接近的规定利润小计。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why the company used its management-defined performance measure in public communications.
examples.zh: 导师问，公司为什么在公开沟通材料中使用「管理层定义的业绩指标」。

collocations: a reconciliation of a management-defined performance measure

words.enDefinition: a reporting section explaining performance and financial condition from management's perspective

examples.en: The sample US filing used management discussion and analysis to explain the change in operating results.
examples.zh: 样本美国申报文件通过「管理层讨论与分析」解释了经营业绩的变化。

examples.en: Our tutor asked what the management discussion and analysis revealed about the company's slow collections.
examples.zh: 导师问，「管理层讨论与分析」透露了哪些关于公司收款缓慢的信息。

collocations: a management discussion and analysis section

words.enDefinition: management's explanation of why it used a measure or choice

examples.en: The report gave management's rationale for showing adjusted operating profit beside the statutory subtotal.
examples.zh: 报告给出了「管理层说明的理由」，解释为何在法定小计旁列出调整后营业利润。

examples.en: We compared management's rationale with the adjustment figures listed below it in the sample report.
examples.zh: 我们把「管理层说明的理由」与样本报告在其下方列出的调整数字作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Assessing how effectively a manager handles the decisions they control

examples.en: The managerial performance evaluation excluded a rent change imposed by head office.
examples.zh: 「管理者绩效评价」排除了总部决定的租金变化。

examples.en: We compared managerial performance evaluation with the separate report on the whole unit.
examples.zh: 我们把「管理者绩效评价」和针对整个单位的单独报告作了比较。

collocations: use financial measures in managerial performance evaluation

words.enDefinition: A policy requiring units to obtain designated items from within the organisation

examples.en: The memo described mandatory internal sourcing for components available from the group's factory.
examples.zh: 备忘录说，集团工厂能供应的零件实行「强制内部采购」。

examples.en: We discussed how mandatory internal sourcing affected the buyer's ability to compare suppliers.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「强制内部采购」如何影响采购方比较供应商。

words.enDefinition: an account that records manufacturing overhead applied to production in a system that tracks actual and allocated overhead separately

examples.en: We credited the manufacturing overhead allocated account when the workshop applied overhead to unfinished jobs.
examples.zh: 车间把制造费用分配给尚未完工的作业时，我们贷记「已分配制造费用账户」。

examples.en: The tutor reconciled the balance in the manufacturing overhead allocated account with total overhead costs incurred.
examples.zh: 导师将「已分配制造费用账户」的余额与实际发生的制造费用总额核对。

collocations: credit the manufacturing overhead allocated account
reconcile the manufacturing overhead allocated account
close the manufacturing overhead allocated account

words.enDefinition: a fall in profit as a share of revenue

examples.en: The case company reported margin contraction as labour costs rose faster than its sales.
examples.zh: 随着人工成本上涨得比销售额快，案例公司报告了「利润率下降」。

examples.en: We discussed how margin contraction could occur even when total sales increased during the quarter.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么季度总销售额增加时仍可能出现「利润率下降」。

words.enDefinition: an increase in profit as a share of revenue

examples.en: The margin expansion came from lower material costs in the fictional manufacturer's main business.
examples.zh: 虚构制造商的主营业务材料成本降低，带来了「利润率上升」。

examples.en: Our group checked whether margin expansion meant the same thing as a rise in total profit.
examples.zh: 小组核对了「利润率上升」和利润总额增加是不是一回事。

words.zhGloss: 以市价为基础的转移价
words.enDefinition: An internal charge based on the price in an outside market
acceptedZhAnswers: 以市价为基础的转移价

examples.en: The model used a market-based transfer price based on independent sales of the same part.
examples.zh: 模型根据同种零件的独立交易，设定了「以市价为基础的转移价」。

examples.en: We checked how a market-based transfer price would change if outside prices fell.
examples.zh: 我们核对了外部价格下跌时，「以市价为基础的转移价」会如何变化。

collocations: compare a market-based transfer price with cost

words.enDefinition: Assumptions independent, informed market participants would apply when pricing an asset or liability.

examples.en: The valuation used market participant assumptions about rental income rather than the owner's own business plans.
examples.zh: 估值采用了关于租金的「市场参与者假设」，未将所有者自己的经营计划作为依据。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the market participant assumptions in the practice valuation were supported by evidence.
examples.zh: 老师问，练习估值中的「市场参与者假设」有没有证据支持。

collocations: a model based on market participant assumptions

words.enDefinition: The sales volume effect of a difference between actual and expected market share, using actual market size and the standard margin.

examples.en: The market share variance was adverse because the shop captured less of the actual market than it expected.
examples.zh: 商店在实际市场上拿到的份额小于预期，因此「市场份额差异」不利。

examples.en: We used the actual industry total for both share figures when calculating the market share variance.
examples.zh: 计算「市场份额差异」时，两个份额的数据都应用于同一个行业实际总量。

collocations: explain the market share variance in the report

words.enDefinition: The sales volume effect of a difference between actual and expected total market size, holding planned share constant and valuing the volume change at standard margin.

examples.en: A bigger total market produced a favourable market size variance even though our expected share stayed unchanged.
examples.zh: 即使预期市场份额未变，更大的市场总规模也带来了有利的「市场规模差异」。

examples.en: We applied the planned share to actual market size before calculating the market size variance in class.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂上先把计划份额应用于实际市场规模，再计算「市场规模差异」。

collocations: isolate the market size variance from market share

words.enDefinition: Information about accounting policies that can influence decisions by primary users when read with the other financial information.

examples.en: The revised note kept material accounting policy information about customer rebates and removed generic descriptions of unrelated policies.
examples.zh: 修订后的附注保留了顾客返利的「重大会计政策信息」，删去了无关政策的通用说明。

examples.en: Our class looked for material accounting policy information that helped readers understand the reported amounts.
examples.zh: 全班查找了有助于读者理解列报金额的「重大会计政策信息」。

collocations: decide what constitutes material accounting policy information

words.enDefinition: A change to a required characteristic or quality of a material used in a product or process.

examples.en: A material specification change meant the folder project needed heavier paper halfway through the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 课堂练习进行到一半，文件夹项目因「材料规格变更」而需用更厚的纸。

examples.en: The case asked whether a material specification change justified revising the allowance for vinyl offcuts.
examples.zh: 案例问的是，发生「材料规格变更」后，是否有必要调整乙烯基材料边角料的定额。

collocations: review the cost impact of a material specification change

words.enDefinition: The difference between actual input used and the standard amount allowed for actual output, valued at standard prices.

examples.en: Extra offcuts increased the material usage variance in our case even though fabric prices stayed the same.
examples.zh: 案例里的布料价格保持稳定，但额外的边角料使「材料用量差异」扩大。

examples.en: The class split the material usage variance into separate mix and yield effects for two types of flour.
examples.zh: 同学们把两种面粉的「材料用量差异」分解为配比影响和产出率影响。

collocations: explain an adverse material usage variance
split the material usage variance into mix and yield

words.enDefinition: Assessing whether omitting, misstating or obscuring information could reasonably be expected to influence primary users' decisions.

examples.en: The class made a materiality judgement before deciding which supplier dispute needed a separate explanation in the note.
examples.zh: 全班先作出「重要性判断」，再确定哪笔供应商争议需要在附注单独说明。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why the nature of an item mattered when making a materiality judgement in the example.
examples.zh: 老师解释了在例题中作「重要性判断」时，为什么项目本身的性质很重要。

collocations: apply a materiality judgement to a disclosure

words.zhGloss: 在工序开始时投入的材料
words.enDefinition: materials introduced at the beginning of a production process rather than gradually during it
acceptedZhAnswers: 在工序开始时投入的材料

examples.en: The problem specified materials added at the start to explain why unfinished units already included paper.
examples.zh: 题目指定了「在工序开始时投入的材料」，说明未完工单位为什么已经包含纸张。

examples.en: We treated materials added at the start as fully included once an item entered the process.
examples.zh: 产品进入工序时，我们就视同「在工序开始时投入的材料」已全部计入该产品。

collocations: assume materials added at the start
costs for materials added at the start
account for materials added at the start

words.enDefinition: Production inputs already held when a decision is being evaluated

examples.en: The worksheet asked whether the materials in stock could be sold instead of used.
examples.zh: 练习表问，现有的「在库材料」是否也可以卖掉。

examples.en: We checked the materials in stock before estimating the additional cash needed.
examples.zh: 我们先核对「在库材料」，再估算所需的额外现金。

collocations: value materials in stock for a decision

words.enDefinition: the release of materials from inventory for use in production or on a job

examples.en: The storekeeper recorded the materials issue when the paper was released for the booklet order.
examples.zh: 纸张领去制作小册子订单时，仓管员记录了这次「材料领发」。

examples.en: We matched the materials issue to the job number before assigning its cost to the order.
examples.zh: 把成本分配给订单前，我们先把「材料领发」记录与作业编号对应起来。

words.enDefinition: The cost effect of changing the proportions of materials, holding total actual input constant and using standard prices.

examples.en: The materials mix variance reflected more wholemeal flour and less white flour in the same total weight.
examples.zh: 「材料配比差异」反映的是总重量一样时，全麦面粉用得更多、白面粉用得更少。

examples.en: We used standard prices in the materials mix variance so a supplier discount would not affect it.
examples.zh: 我们计算「材料配比差异」时用标准价格，这样供应商折扣就不会影响结果。

collocations: separate the materials mix variance from yield

words.enDefinition: The cost effect of paying a different material price from the standard, measured at the relevant actual quantity.

examples.en: The exercise recognised the materials price variance when the workshop bought the paper, before production began.
examples.zh: 练习在工场买入纸张、生产尚未开始时确认「材料价格差异」。

examples.en: The materials price variance changed after a corrected invoice showed a lower price per kilogram of flour.
examples.zh: 更正后的发票显示每公斤面粉价格更低，「材料价格差异」随之改变。

collocations: recognise the materials price variance at purchase

words.enDefinition: a form requesting materials from stores and recording which work will use them

examples.en: I entered the job number on the materials requisition form before collecting the fabric.
examples.zh: 去领布料前，我在「领料单」上填了作业编号。

examples.en: The materials requisition form showed that the printing job used two different weights of paper.
examples.zh: 「领料单」显示，印刷作业用了两种不同克重的纸。

collocations: match a materials requisition form to a job

words.enDefinition: The cost effect of getting more or less output from total actual input than the standard yield implies, valued at standard mix costs.

examples.en: The materials yield variance showed that the same weight of dough produced fewer saleable rolls than expected.
examples.zh: 「材料产出率差异」表明同样重量的面团做出的可售面包卷少于预期。

examples.en: We checked the materials yield variance separately after measuring the effect of using a different blend.
examples.zh: 量化不同配方带来的影响之后，我们单独核对了「材料产出率差异」。

collocations: explain a favourable materials yield variance
separate the materials yield variance from mix

words.enDefinition: The most that buyers are expected to order during a period

examples.en: The model stopped producing each item once its maximum demand was met.
examples.zh: 每种商品达到「需求量上限」后，模型就停止安排生产。

examples.en: We checked maximum demand before giving the remaining hours to another product.
examples.zh: 我们先核对了「需求量上限」，再把剩余工时分给另一款产品。

words.zhGloss: 最高可接受内部转移价
words.enDefinition: The highest internal charge acceptable to the receiving division
acceptedZhAnswers: 最高可接受内部转移价

examples.en: A cheaper outside offer lowered the maximum transfer price in our classroom case.
examples.zh: 在课堂案例里，较低的外部报价降低了「最高可接受内部转移价」。

examples.en: We calculated the maximum transfer price from the receiving unit's available alternatives.
examples.zh: 我们根据接收单位可选的其他方案，计算了「最高可接受内部转移价」。

collocations: a maximum transfer price for the buyer

words.enDefinition: an explanation of what a measure includes and represents

examples.en: We read the measure definition before comparing adjusted profit across the two sample reports.
examples.zh: 我们先读了「指标定义」，再比较两份样本报告里的调整后利润。

examples.en: The fictional report put the measure definition beneath the table showing three years of results.
examples.zh: 虚构报告把「指标定义」放在三年业绩表的下方。

collocations: a change to the measure definition

words.enDefinition: Under IFRS 15, a measure of how much of an over-time performance obligation has been satisfied.

examples.en: The notes explained why hours of support delivered provided a reasonable measure of progress in the example.
examples.zh: 附注解释了为什么例题中已提供支持服务的工时是合理的「履约进度计量指标」。

examples.en: Our group used the measure of progress to calculate the revenue earned by the end of June.
examples.zh: 我们组用「履约进度计量指标」计算截至六月底已赚取的收入。

collocations: apply a measure of progress consistently

words.enDefinition: The specified feature used to determine a reported amount, such as historical cost or fair value.

examples.en: The accounting policy note identified the measurement basis for each category of equipment in the report.
examples.zh: 报告的会计政策附注列明了各类设备所用的「计量基础」。

examples.en: We highlighted the measurement basis before comparing amounts for the same type of property across companies.
examples.zh: 比较各公司同类物业的账面金额之前，我们先标出了「计量基础」。

words.enDefinition: Uncertainty that arises when a reported amount cannot be observed directly and must be estimated.

examples.en: The estimates note explained the measurement uncertainty around the future cost of restoring the leased site.
examples.zh: 估计事项附注解释了租用场地未来恢复成本的「计量不确定性」。

examples.en: The class discussed measurement uncertainty because available prices could not directly establish the equipment's fair value.
examples.zh: 现有价格无法直接确定设备的公允价值，大家因此讨论了「计量不确定性」。

collocations: a high degree of measurement uncertainty

words.enDefinition: A target amount of cash that an organisation wants to retain at the end of a period.

examples.en: The exercise required a minimum cash balance even after the workshop paid its suppliers in June.
examples.zh: 练习要求工场在六月向供应商付款后仍保持「最低现金储备余额」。

examples.en: Our group compared the expected ending cash with the minimum cash balance set by the committee.
examples.zh: 我们小组把预计期末现金与委员会设定的「最低现金储备余额」作了比较。

collocations: compare ending cash with the minimum cash balance

words.enDefinition: An agreement to buy at least a specified quantity or value

examples.en: The outside quote included a minimum purchase commitment that affected the comparison.
examples.zh: 外部报价含「最低采购承诺」，这对方案对比有影响。

examples.en: We estimated inventory needs before evaluating the minimum purchase commitment in the contract.
examples.zh: 评估合同中的「最低采购承诺」前，我们估算了库存需求。

collocations: agree to a minimum purchase commitment
factor in a minimum purchase commitment

words.enDefinition: The lowest acceptable percentage return on a defined investment base

examples.en: The tutor set a minimum required return for both divisions in the model.
examples.zh: 导师在模型中给两个分部都设定了「最低必要报酬率」。

examples.en: We multiplied the minimum required return by the asset base in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，我们把「最低必要报酬率」乘以资产基数。

words.enDefinition: The lowest price covering the additional and opportunity costs of acceptance

examples.en: We checked the minimum special order price after adding a separate delivery cost.
examples.zh: 我们加入单独的配送费后，核对了「特殊订单最低接受价」。

examples.en: The case raised the minimum special order price when serving regular customers became impossible.
examples.zh: 接了订单就无法服务常规顾客时，案例提高了「特殊订单最低接受价」。

collocations: calculate the minimum special order price
compare the minimum special order price with the offer
quote a minimum special order price

words.zhGloss: 最低可接受内部转移价
words.enDefinition: The lowest internal charge acceptable to the supplying division
acceptedZhAnswers: 最低可接受内部转移价

examples.en: The minimum transfer price increased after the transfer would displace some outside sales.
examples.zh: 当内部调拨会挤占部分对外销售时，「最低可接受内部转移价」提高了。

examples.en: Our worksheet calculated a minimum transfer price for the division supplying the components.
examples.zh: 练习表算出了供应零件的分部的「最低可接受内部转移价」。

collocations: compare the minimum transfer price with an offer

words.enDefinition: The change in a total caused by different proportions of products or inputs at a given overall quantity.

examples.en: The mix effect explained why contribution rose even though the stall sold the same total number of mugs.
examples.zh: 摊位卖出的杯子总数不变，而「组合效应」解释了边际贡献为什么会上升。

examples.en: We isolated the mix effect before calculating what the higher total input had cost the bakery.
examples.zh: 我们先单独量化「组合效应」，再计算总投入增加让烘焙店多花了多少钱。

collocations: separate the mix effect from total volume

words.enDefinition: The accessible market with the best net proceeds or lowest net transfer cost after transaction and transport costs.

examples.en: With no principal market identified, we compared accessible exchanges to find the most advantageous market.
examples.zh: 未找到主要市场时，我们对比了可进入的交易场所，以确定「最有利市场」。

examples.en: Our tutor deducted selling and transport costs when comparing the alternatives for the most advantageous market.
examples.zh: 老师比较各个候选市场时扣除了销售及运输成本，以确定「最有利市场」。

collocations: use the most advantageous market when no principal market exists

words.zhGloss: 最直接可比的准则指标
words.enDefinition: the closest GAAP measure to which a US non-GAAP measure is compared
acceptedZhAnswers: 最直接可比的准则指标
acceptedEnVariants: most directly comparable GAAP financial measure

examples.en: The sample reconciliation started with the most directly comparable GAAP measure from the income statement.
examples.zh: 样本调节表从利润表中的「最直接可比的准则指标」开始。

examples.en: We checked whether the sample chose operating profit as the most directly comparable GAAP measure.
examples.zh: 我们核对了样本是否把营业利润选为「最直接可比的准则指标」。

collocations: identify the most directly comparable GAAP measure
reconcile to the most directly comparable GAAP measure
present the most directly comparable GAAP measure

words.enDefinition: the specified subtotal closest to an alternative measure being reconciled

examples.en: The IFRS example used operating profit as the most directly comparable subtotal for the adjusted measure.
examples.zh: IFRS 示例以营业利润作为调整后指标的「最直接可比的小计」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to find the most directly comparable subtotal in the sample reconciliation.
examples.zh: 导师让我们在样本调节表中找出「最直接可比的小计」。

collocations: identify the most directly comparable subtotal
reconcile to the most directly comparable subtotal
present the most directly comparable subtotal

words.enDefinition: changes in the balances of liabilities arising from expenses that have been recorded and remain payable

examples.en: The largest movements in accrued liabilities reflected unpaid wages and estimated electricity costs at quarter end.
examples.zh: 「应计负债变动」中金额最大的是季末尚未支付的工资和预估电费。

examples.en: We analysed movements in accrued liabilities to understand why cash payments differed from recorded expenses that year.
examples.zh: 我们分析了「应计负债变动」，以弄清本年现金付款额为何与账面费用不同。

collocations: adjust for movements in accrued liabilities

words.enDefinition: A written explanation in financial reporting that describes facts, judgements or uncertainties in words.

examples.en: The narrative disclosure explained why the two valuation methods produced different results for the same property.
examples.zh: 「文字说明式披露」解释了为什么两种估值方法对同一物业得出不同的结果。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to add narrative disclosure about the timetable below the table of expected payments.
examples.zh: 老师让我们在预计付款表下补充关于时间安排的「文字说明式披露」。

collocations: accompany a table with narrative disclosure

words.zhGloss: 协商确定的内部转移价
words.enDefinition: An internal charge agreed by the divisions exchanging goods or services
acceptedZhAnswers: 协商确定的内部转移价

examples.en: Both managers signed off on a negotiated transfer price for the next batch.
examples.zh: 两位经理都批准了下一批的「协商确定的内部转移价」。

examples.en: The case compared a negotiated transfer price with the rate stipulated by management.
examples.zh: 案例将「协商确定的内部转移价」与管理层规定的费率作了对照。

collocations: agree on a negotiated transfer price

words.enDefinition: The organisation's gain from an internal transfer after relevant costs

examples.en: The case calculated the net benefit of internal transfer using only costs that would actually change.
examples.zh: 案例只用实际会发生变动的成本计算「内部调拨净收益」。

examples.en: Our group checked the net benefit of internal transfer after losing a potential outside sale.
examples.zh: 失去一笔潜在的对外销售后，我们组核对了「内部调拨净收益」。

collocations: calculate the net benefit of internal transfer
compare the net benefit of internal transfer
a positive net benefit of internal transfer

words.enDefinition: Measuring assets after subtracting recorded depreciation from their recorded cost

examples.en: The worksheet used a net book value basis for both factories' equipment figures.
examples.zh: 练习表里的两个工厂都用「账面净值口径」计算设备数值。

examples.en: We checked how the net book value basis affected a division with older assets.
examples.zh: 我们核对「账面净值口径」怎样影响拥有较旧资产的分部。

collocations: calculate assets on a net book value basis
a return measured on a net book value basis
use a net book value basis

examples.en: The exercise subtracted operating liabilities from operating assets to arrive at net operating assets.
examples.zh: 练习用经营资产减去经营负债，求出「净经营资产」。

examples.en: Our group checked which balances the fictional analyst treated as operating before calculating net operating assets.
examples.zh: 小组先确认虚构分析员把哪些余额视为经营性项目，再计算「净经营资产」。

words.enDefinition: operating profit after an estimated tax charge on operating income

examples.en: The tutor showed how the assumed tax rate affected the calculation of net operating profit after tax.

examples.en: The worksheet used the net realizable value method because neither output had an observable split-off price.
examples.zh: 两项产出都没有可观察的分离点价格，练习表用了「可变现净值分配法」。

examples.en: We compared the net realizable value method with an allocation based on the weight of each output.
examples.zh: 我们把「可变现净值分配法」与根据各项产出重量做的分配作了比较。

words.enDefinition: The cost reduction after accounting for relevant expenses of external supply

examples.en: The model showed net savings from outsourcing even after adding the supplier's delivery charge.
examples.zh: 即使加上供货商的配送费，模型也显示存在「外包节省的净成本」。

examples.en: We checked whether net savings from outsourcing changed if employees could switch to other work.
examples.zh: 我们核对了员工若转去做其他工作，「外包节省的净成本」会不会变化。

collocations: review projected net savings from outsourcing

words.enDefinition: The overall difference after favourable and adverse components have been combined with the appropriate signs.

examples.en: The net variance was close to zero because lower paint prices almost cancelled the cost of extra paint.
examples.zh: 油漆降价几乎抵消了多耗油漆的成本，因此「净差异」接近零。

examples.en: We calculated the net variance after checking which lines were favourable and which ones were adverse.
examples.zh: 我们核对了哪些行是有利差异、哪些是不利差异，再计算「净差异」。

words.enDefinition: lease payment obligations recognised for leases beginning during the reporting period

examples.en: The accountant identified new lease liabilities when the company's rented delivery vehicles first became available for use.

examples.en: The practice schedule showed the recognition of new lease liabilities separately from cash paid against existing balances.
examples.zh: 练习附表把「新增租赁负债」的确认与为偿还现有负债付出的现金分开列报。

words.enDefinition: Issued standards that are not mandatory for the entity's current reporting period.

examples.en: The sample note on new standards not yet effective described what the company expected to change next year.
examples.zh: 示例里的「尚未生效的新准则」附注说明了公司预计下一年在哪些方面发生变化。

examples.en: The class looked for new standards not yet effective in the first section of the accounting policies note.
examples.zh: 同学们在会计政策附注的第一节查找「尚未生效的新准则」。

collocations: identify new standards not yet effective

words.enDefinition: An event after the period indicating a condition arising after the reporting date.

examples.zh: 练习把年末后发生的火灾列为「日后非调整事项」，并说明其影响。

examples.en: The tutor asked which note should describe the non-adjusting event and its estimated financial effect.

examples.en: We distinguished non-cash changes in financing liabilities from repayments that reduced the same balances during the year.
examples.zh: 我们将「筹资活动产生的负债的非现金变动」与本年使同一余额减少的还款区分开。

disclose non-cash changes in financing liabilities
explain non-cash changes in financing liabilities

words.enDefinition: something of value transferred or promised in an exchange in a form other than cash or cash equivalents

examples.en: The buyer offered new shares as non-cash consideration when it agreed to purchase the software business.
examples.zh: 买方同意收购这家软件企业时，提出用新股作为「非现金对价」。

examples.en: We compared the cash paid at completion with the non-cash consideration described in the acquisition note.
examples.zh: 我们比较了交割时支付的现金和收购附注说明的「非现金对价」。

words.enDefinition: an expense recognised in profit or loss without an accompanying payment of cash at recognition

examples.en: Depreciation was the largest non-cash expense in the report from the company that owned the equipment.
examples.zh: 在设备所有方的报告里，折旧是金额最大的「非现金费用」。

examples.en: We added back the non-cash expense so the write-down would not reduce the operating cash total.
examples.zh: 我们加回了这项「非现金费用」，这样资产减记就不会压低经营现金总额。

words.enDefinition: a transaction affecting an entity's borrowings or contributed equity without an accompanying cash flow

examples.en: A non-cash financing activity took place when the lenders accepted new shares in exchange for their debt claims.
examples.zh: 贷款机构同意以债权换取新股时，发生了一项「非现金筹资活动」。

examples.en: The company disclosed a non-cash financing activity after signing a lease without making an immediate cash payment.
examples.zh: 公司签下租约并确认有关负债时没有立即付现，因此披露了一项「非现金筹资活动」。

collocations: report a non-cash financing activity in the notes

words.enDefinition: income recognised without receiving cash at the point when the income is recorded

examples.en: The analyst excluded non-cash income from the operating cash estimate because it reflected an unrealised gain.
examples.zh: 分析员把「非现金收益」从经营现金估算中剔除，因为它反映的是未实现利得。

examples.en: The note explained why the reported non-cash income had no effect on the company's cash receipts.
examples.zh: 附注解释了报告中的「非现金收益」为什么没有影响公司的收款。

words.enDefinition: an investing transaction that does not require an inflow or outflow of cash or cash equivalents at the time

examples.en: The case described a non-cash investing activity in which a company exchanged its shares for a building.
examples.zh: 这个案例描述一项「非现金投资活动」，即一家公司用自己的股份换取一栋建筑。

examples.en: We found the non-cash investing activity in the notes because the parties exchanged equipment without paying cash.
examples.zh: 我们在附注中找到这项「非现金投资活动」，因为双方互换设备，没有支付现金。

collocations: exclude a non-cash investing activity from cash flows

words.zhGloss: 非公认会计准则财务指标

acceptedZhAnswers: 非公认会计准则财务指标

examples.en: The sample earnings release presented a non-GAAP financial measure beside the closest figure calculated under GAAP.
examples.zh: 样本业绩公告把「非公认会计准则财务指标」列在按公认会计准则计算的最接近数字旁。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which adjustments separated the non-GAAP financial measure from the reported GAAP result.
examples.zh: 导师问，「非公认会计准则财务指标」与列报的公认会计准则结果之间有哪些调整。

collocations: a non-GAAP financial measure in an earnings release

words.enDefinition: an item categorised outside operating results under a stated basis

examples.en: The worksheet treated interest income as a non-operating item for the sample manufacturing company.
examples.zh: 对这家样本制造商，练习表把利息收入视为「非经营性项目」。

examples.en: We checked the notes before treating the same transaction as a non-operating item in both samples.
examples.zh: 在两个样本中都把同一交易视为「非经营性项目」之前，我们先核对了附注。

words.enDefinition: a cash movement unlikely to repeat under ordinary conditions

examples.en: The tutor identified a non-recurring cash flow after the sample company sold its old premises.
examples.zh: 样本公司出售原经营场地后，导师识别出了一笔「非经常性现金流」。

examples.en: Our group separated the non-recurring cash flow before comparing the business's usual cash generation.
examples.zh: 小组先将「非经常性现金流」单列，再比较企业日常产生现金的情况。

words.enDefinition: an income or expense item not expected to arise regularly

examples.en: The example treated the gain from selling an old warehouse as a non-recurring item.
examples.zh: 示例把出售旧仓库的收益视为「非经常性项目」。

examples.en: Our tutor checked whether an item described as a non-recurring item had appeared in earlier reports.
examples.zh: 导师核对了被称为「非经常性项目」的事项是否也出现在更早的报告里。

collocations: an adjustment for a non-recurring item

words.enDefinition: an activity that uses resources without increasing the value of the output for its customer

examples.en: The workshop identified moving the same box twice as a non-value-added activity in its process.
examples.zh: 工作室把流程里同一箱子搬两遍视为「不增值作业」。

examples.en: We discussed whether the non-value-added activity was still necessary because of the way records were kept.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了，考虑到现在的记录方式，那项「不增值作业」是否仍然必需。

words.enDefinition: A consideration such as quality or reliability not directly measured in money

examples.en: The team recorded delivery reliability as a nonfinancial factor in its comparison.
examples.zh: 团队把交货可靠性记录为对比中的一项「非财务因素」。

examples.en: A nonfinancial factor mattered when the two options produced identical cost estimates.
examples.zh: 两种方案的成本估算完全相同时，一项「非财务因素」影响了判断。

words.enDefinition: a cost not arising from the production of goods, such as selling or general administration costs

examples.en: The class classified the fee for advertising the booklets as a nonmanufacturing cost in the example.
examples.zh: 课堂把示例中给小册子做广告的费用归为「非制造成本」。

examples.en: The sample report listed a nonmanufacturing cost for advertising below the cost of goods sold.
examples.zh: 示例报告在销售成本下方列了一项广告费，属于「非制造成本」。

collocations: exclude nonmanufacturing costs from product inventory

words.enDefinition: the average output expected under normal conditions over several periods, allowing for planned interruptions

examples.en: We estimated normal capacity from several years of typical output, allowing for scheduled maintenance.
examples.zh: 我们用几年的典型产量估算「正常生产能力」，并考虑了计划内维护。

examples.en: The lecturer compared normal capacity with output from an unusually quiet month in the workshop.
examples.zh: 讲师把「正常生产能力」与工作室特别清闲的一个月的产量作了比较。

collocations: allocate costs based on normal capacity

words.enDefinition: a method assigning actual direct costs to output and applying overhead using a predetermined rate

examples.en: The shop used normal costing to charge actual paper costs and apply overhead at its predetermined rate.
examples.zh: 车间采用「正常成本法」，按实际金额计入纸张成本，按预定费率分配制造费用。

examples.en: Our tutor explained how normal costing let managers estimate job costs before actual overhead was known.
examples.zh: 导师解释了管理者如何在实际间接费用尚未确定时，用「正常成本法」估算作业成本。

words.enDefinition: spoilage expected under usual efficient operating conditions in a production process

examples.en: The workshop budget allowed for normal spoilage when several printed covers might come out unusable.
examples.zh: 工作室预算允许出现「正常废品损失」，因为可能有几张印出的封面不能用。

examples.en: We treated the small number of torn labels as normal spoilage in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 课堂练习中，我们把少数破损标签当作「正常废品损失」。

words.enDefinition: earnings adjusted to approximate results under ordinary conditions

examples.en: Our worksheet estimated normalised earnings after removing the assumed impact of a temporary closure.
examples.zh: 练习表剔除假定的临时停业影响后，估算了「常态化盈利」。

examples.en: The tutor asked which assumptions supported the normalised earnings figure in the sample analysis.
examples.zh: 导师问，样本分析中「常态化盈利」的数字基于哪些假设。

words.enDefinition: A number or label beside a reported item directing readers to its related financial statement note.

examples.en: I followed the note reference beside the property balance to find a breakdown of the total.
examples.zh: 我顺着物业余额旁的「附注编号」找到了总额明细。

examples.en: The note reference next to the provision line matched the number at the top of the supporting table.
examples.zh: 预计负债项目旁的「附注编号」和明细表顶部的编号一致。

collocations: insert a note reference next to a line item

words.enDefinition: Information accompanying the primary statements that explains reported amounts, accounting policies and other relevant matters.

examples.en: We read the notes to the financial statements to find out what caused the increase in provisions.
examples.zh: 我们读了「财务报表附注」，了解预计负债增加的原因。

examples.en: The notes to the financial statements explained which expenses were included in each category in the table.
examples.zh: 「财务报表附注」解释了表格里每一类包含哪些费用。

collocations: read the notes to the financial statements
include information in the notes to the financial statements
refer to the notes to the financial statements

words.enDefinition: Under IAS 37, a past event creating a legal or constructive obligation with no realistic alternative to settlement.

examples.en: In the example, the obligating event was installing equipment that the company had committed to remove later.
examples.zh: 例题中的「义务形成事项」是安装设备，因为公司已经承诺之后会将设备拆除。

examples.en: The tutor asked which obligating event had occurred before the closing date in the accounting case.
examples.zh: 老师问，会计例题中什么「义务形成事项」已在结账日前发生。

collocations: the date of the obligating event

words.enDefinition: Presenting material information so unclearly that its effect is similar to omitting or misstating it.

examples.en: The class removed unrelated details from the note to avoid obscuring material information about the large provision.
examples.zh: 为了避免「使重要信息难以辨识」，全班删去了大额预计负债附注中无关的细节。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed obscuring material information when key explanations appeared in several unrelated parts of the report.
examples.zh: 关键说明散在报告几个无关位置，老师因此讨论了「使重要信息难以辨识」的问题。

collocations: identify wording that is obscuring material information

words.enDefinition: Valuation variables developed from market data that reflect assumptions used by market participants.

examples.en: We used observable inputs from recent comparable sales to estimate the value of the practice building.
examples.zh: 我们用近期可比交易中的「可观察输入值」估算例题建筑物的价值。

examples.en: The note identified observable inputs from public markets even though the asset itself was not traded there.
examples.zh: 虽然该资产本身未在公开市场交易，附注仍列出了源自公开市场的「可观察输入值」。

collocations: give priority to relevant observable inputs

words.enDefinition: Presenting assets against liabilities or income against expenses as a single net amount under applicable rules.

examples.en: The class discussed offsetting after noticing that the example statement showed one net amount for two balances.
examples.zh: 发现示例报表用一个净额列示两个余额后，全班讨论了「抵销列报」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which conditions would permit offsetting the two financial instruments in the classroom case.
examples.zh: 老师问，课堂例题中哪些条件允许对这两项金融工具作「抵销列报」。

words.enDefinition: Two or more variances with opposing effects that reduce the effect of one another when combined.

examples.en: The small total hid offsetting variances from cheaper fabric and extra fabric used in the workshop.
examples.zh: 总差异看起来很小，却掩盖了布料变便宜和工场布料用量增加形成的「相互抵消的差异」。

examples.en: Our tutor wanted offsetting variances shown separately so the class could see what happened in each department.
examples.zh: 老师希望分别列出「相互抵消的差异」，让大家了解各个部门发生了什么。

words.enDefinition: using the same definitions or calculation methods throughout a comparison

examples.en: The sample table reported both years on a consistent basis after changing the expense categories.
examples.zh: 样本表在调整费用类别后，仍「按一致口径」报告两年的数据。

examples.en: Our group recalculated the figures on a consistent basis before comparing the two margins shown.
examples.zh: 小组先「按一致口径」重算数据，再比较表上的两个利润率。

collocations: report figures on a consistent basis
measure results on a consistent basis
compare years on a consistent basis

words.enDefinition: A difference between plan and outcome caused by an event not expected to repeat in the normal periods ahead.

examples.en: The one-off variance came from replacing a broken window in the practice workshop late in term.
examples.zh: 学期快结束时，模拟工场换了一扇坏窗，产生了「一次性差异」。

examples.en: We excluded the one-off variance when discussing the usual monthly cost of operating the rehearsal room.
examples.zh: 讨论排练室通常的月度运行成本时，我们剔除了这项「一次性差异」。

collocations: identify a one-off variance in spending

words.enDefinition: A preparation fee incurred once rather than for every unit

examples.en: The supplier put a one-time setup charge beside the price per printed bag.
examples.zh: 供应商在印花包单价旁另列了「一次性准备费」。

examples.en: The case kept the one-time setup charge constant as order volume increased.
examples.zh: 案例里，订单量增加时，「一次性准备费」保持不变。

words.enDefinition: Under IAS 37, a contract whose unavoidable costs exceed the expected economic benefits from it.

examples.en: The worksheet showed an onerous contract because the unavoidable costs exceeded the benefits expected from the order.
examples.zh: 未能避免的成本超过这笔订单的预期经济利益，练习表因此列出一项「亏损合同」。

examples.en: The tutor asked why the arrangement became an onerous contract after the supplier increased material prices.
examples.zh: 老师问，供应商提高材料价格之后，这项安排为什么成了「亏损合同」。

collocations: recognise a provision for an onerous contract
assess whether a contract is an onerous contract

words.enDefinition: explaining the change between the cash balances at the start and end of a cash flow statement

examples.en: The accountant completed the opening and closing cash reconciliation after incorporating the exchange rate effect for the year.
examples.zh: 纳入全年汇率变动的影响后，会计完成了「期初与期末现金调节」。

examples.en: Our worksheet used an opening and closing cash reconciliation to show the source of the reported cash movement.
examples.zh: 我们的练习表用「期初与期末现金调节」说明报告中现金变动的来源。

collocations: prepare an opening and closing cash reconciliation
check the opening and closing cash reconciliation
publish an opening and closing cash reconciliation

words.zhGloss: 期初现金及现金等价物
words.enDefinition: the reported cash and cash equivalents balance at the beginning of a period
acceptedZhAnswers: 期初现金及现金等价物

examples.en: The accountant entered opening cash and cash equivalents before adding the movements for the year.
examples.zh: 会计先填入「期初现金及现金等价物」，再加上全年的各项变动。

examples.en: We checked that opening cash and cash equivalents agreed with the last period's closing figure.
examples.zh: 我们核对了「期初现金及现金等价物」是否与上一期期末金额一致。

collocations: report opening cash and cash equivalents
verify opening cash and cash equivalents
compare opening cash and cash equivalents with prior-year figures

words.enDefinition: the amount of receivables outstanding at the beginning of the period covered by a schedule

examples.en: The opening receivables balance matched the prior year's closing figure in the statement we were given.
examples.zh: 在发给我们的报表中，「期初应收账款余额」与上一年度的期末金额相等。

examples.en: We started with the opening receivables balance before adding the value of invoices raised during the period.
examples.zh: 我们从「期初应收账款余额」开始算，再加上本期开具发票的金额。

collocations: carry forward the opening receivables balance

words.enDefinition: A statement of financial position as of the beginning of a period, presented in specified circumstances.

examples.en: The first-time IFRS exercise began with an opening statement of financial position at the date of transition.
examples.zh: 首次采用国际财务报告准则的练习先编制了转换日的「期初财务状况表」。

examples.en: The tutor explained why the restatement example included an opening statement of financial position for the comparative period.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么重述例题包含比较期间开始日的「期初财务状况表」。

collocations: prepare an opening statement of financial position
an opening statement of financial position at transition
present an opening statement of financial position

words.enDefinition: Use all available production capacity during the period being considered

examples.en: The case assumed both presses would operate at full capacity before the new order arrived.
examples.zh: 案例假设，新订单到来之前，两台印刷机都将「满负荷运行」。

examples.en: If the machines operate at full capacity, the sample shop would need another shift.
examples.zh: 如果机器已经「满负荷运行」，示例商店就需要再加一个班次。

collocations: continue to operate at full capacity
expect to operate at full capacity
plan to operate at full capacity

words.enDefinition: the main revenue-producing activities of an entity and activities outside the investing and financing categories

examples.en: The report separated cash flows from operating activities from the proceeds of the equipment sale.
examples.zh: 报告把「经营活动」产生的现金流与出售设备所得分开列示。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why ordinary customer collections appeared under operating activities in the statement.
examples.zh: 导师问，为什么对顾客的日常收款列在报表的「经营活动」下。

collocations: classify a payment under operating activities

words.enDefinition: The measured value of operating assets included in a performance calculation

examples.en: The case changed the operating asset base to exclude an unused building.
examples.zh: 案例调整了「经营资产基数」，扣掉了一栋闲置建筑。

examples.en: We compared two versions of the operating asset base in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂练习中比较了「经营资产基数」的两种计算口径。

words.enDefinition: cash flow from operations expressed as a percentage of revenue

examples.en: The worksheet divided operating cash flow by revenue to calculate the operating cash flow margin.
examples.zh: 练习表用经营现金流除以收入，计算「经营现金流利润率」。

examples.en: The tutor asked why operating cash flow margin and accounting profit margin could move in different directions.
examples.zh: 导师问，为什么「经营现金流利润率」与会计利润率的变动方向可能不同。

collocations: a higher operating cash flow margin

words.enDefinition: cash received from an entity's operating activities

examples.en: The first operating cash inflow on the schedule came from collecting earlier customer invoices.
examples.zh: 表上的第一笔「经营现金流入」来自收回之前开票的顾客款项。

examples.en: We traced the largest operating cash inflow to the receipts recorded at the service counter.
examples.zh: 我们把最大的一笔「经营现金流入」追溯到服务台记录的实收款项。

words.enDefinition: cash paid in connection with an entity's operating activities

examples.en: The report showed an operating cash outflow when the workshop paid its monthly electricity bill.
examples.zh: 工作室支付每月电费时，报告中出现了一笔「经营现金流出」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the wages paid were an operating cash outflow in the example.
examples.zh: 导师问，例中支付的工资是否属于「经营现金流出」。

words.enDefinition: the time from acquiring inventory to collecting cash from sales

examples.en: The sample operating cycle began when the retailer acquired inventory and ended when customers paid.
examples.zh: 样本的「营业周期」从零售商取得存货开始，到顾客付款结束。

examples.en: The tutor compared the operating cycle of a fast-selling shop with that of a furniture maker.
examples.zh: 导师比较了销售速度快的商店与一家家具制造商的「营业周期」。

words.enDefinition: operating profit expressed as a share of revenue

examples.en: The classroom calculation divided operating profit by revenue to find the operating margin.
examples.zh: 课堂用营业利润除以收入计算「营业利润率」。

examples.en: We compared operating margin under the same definitions before discussing the two stores' rent costs.
examples.zh: 我们先按相同定义比较「营业利润率」，再讨论两家商店的租金成本。

words.enDefinition: short-term operating assets less short-term operating liabilities under a stated definition

examples.en: The worksheet calculated operating working capital from inventory, trade receivables, and trade payables in the simplified case.
examples.zh: 在简化案例中，练习表根据存货、应收账款和应付账款计算「经营性营运资金」。

examples.en: We checked whether the sample analyst excluded cash and borrowing from operating working capital.
examples.zh: 我们核对了样本分析员是否将现金和借款排除在「经营性营运资金」之外。

collocations: a measure of operating working capital

words.zhGloss: 工序与分批结合的成本法
words.enDefinition: a hybrid costing system combining job costing for some inputs with process costing for common operations
acceptedZhAnswers: 工序与分批结合的成本法

examples.en: The shoe example used operation costing because each batch used different fabric but followed identical assembly steps.
examples.zh: 示例中的鞋采用「工序与分批结合的成本法」，各批用料不同，组装步骤一致。

examples.en: Our lecturer compared operation costing with process costing for products made entirely from the same materials.
examples.zh: 讲师把「工序与分批结合的成本法」与所有产品原材料完全相同情况下用的分步成本法作了比较。

words.enDefinition: The part of a variance measured by comparing actual performance with a revised budget or standard.

examples.en: The operational variance came from comparing actual paper use with the allowance under the revised production standard.
examples.zh: 「运营差异」来自实际用纸量与修订后生产标准所允许用量的比较。

examples.en: Our tutor found the operational variance by comparing the realised selling price with the revised standard price.
examples.zh: 老师通过比较实际成交价与修订后的标准售价，得出了「运营差异」。

words.enDefinition: The value of the best alternative use of committed capacity

examples.en: The opportunity cost of capacity came from jobs the workshop would have to turn away.
examples.zh: 「产能机会成本」来自工作室必须婉拒的订单。

examples.en: Our example showed no opportunity cost of capacity while an unused machine remained available.
examples.zh: 范例中还有闲置机器可用，因而没有「产能机会成本」。

collocations: estimate the opportunity cost of capacity
include the opportunity cost of capacity

words.enDefinition: The production combination giving the best result under stated constraints

examples.en: The optimal product mix used all the printing time available in the example.
examples.zh: 该示例中的「最优产品组合」用完了所有可用打印时间。

examples.en: We calculated another optimal product mix after finding that the maximum demand for posters was lower than expected.
examples.zh: 发现海报需求上限低于预期后，我们重新算了一种「最优产品组合」。

collocations: constraints on the optimal product mix

words.enDefinition: A market transaction allowing usual exposure and marketing, without a forced sale or distress liquidation.

examples.en: The valuation exercise treated the sale as an orderly transaction because the equipment had been marketed normally.
examples.zh: 估值练习将这笔出售视为「有序交易」，因为设备已经过正常的市场推介。

examples.en: Our tutor questioned whether an immediate forced sale could provide the price of an orderly transaction.
examples.zh: 老师问，迫于压力立即出售的价格能否代表「有序交易」的价格。

words.enDefinition: revenue growth adjusted for acquisitions and other specified external effects

examples.en: The sample calculated organic revenue growth after excluding the contribution from a newly acquired business.
examples.zh: 样本剔除了新收购业务的贡献后，再计算「有机收入增长」。

examples.en: We read the note defining organic revenue growth to see which additional effects were excluded.
examples.zh: 我们阅读了定义「有机收入增长」的附注，查看还剔除了哪些影响。

collocations: the definition of organic revenue growth

words.enDefinition: The budget initially set for a period, used as a reference when analysing revisions or results.

examples.en: The original budget assumed both repair desks would remain open throughout the autumn term.
examples.zh: 「最初的预算」假设两个维修服务台整个秋季学期都会开放。

examples.en: We used the original budget as a reference when reviewing the updated estimates for next month.
examples.zh: 审查下月更新的估算时，我们以「最初的预算」为参考。

words.enDefinition: Uncertainty about the amount or timing of future inflows or outflows arising from an asset or liability.

examples.en: There was outcome uncertainty because the repair obligation existed but the timing of payments was unclear.
examples.zh: 维修义务已经存在，但付款时间不清楚，因此有「结果不确定性」。

examples.en: Our report described outcome uncertainty for the receivables even though we knew the customers owed the money.
examples.zh: 虽然我们知道顾客确实欠款，报告仍说明了这些应收款的「结果不确定性」。

words.enDefinition: The amount an external seller quotes for supplying an item

examples.en: The outside supplier price included packaging that the internal unit could provide itself.
examples.zh: 「外部供应商报价」包括内部单位可自行提供的包装。

examples.en: We checked whether the outside supplier price included delivery to the receiving division.
examples.zh: 我们核对了「外部供应商报价」是否包括往接收分部配送的费用。

collocations: an outside supplier price for the part

words.zhGloss: 在一段时间内确认收入
words.enDefinition: Recognising revenue as the entity satisfies a performance obligation over a period rather than on a single date.
acceptedZhAnswers: 在一段时间内确认收入

examples.en: The case used over-time revenue recognition for support that customers received throughout the six-month service agreement.
examples.zh: 顾客在六个月的服务协议期内持续获得支持，例题因此采用「在一段时间内确认收入」。

examples.en: We checked the reported measure of progress before interpreting over-time revenue recognition in the sample notes.
examples.zh: 我们先查看列报的履约进度计量方法，再解读示例附注如何「在一段时间内确认收入」。

collocations: assess eligibility for over-time revenue recognition
explain the method for over-time revenue recognition

words.enDefinition: the process of charging production overhead to units using an absorption rate or other allocation basis

examples.en: The exercise showed overhead absorption into product costs before we calculated the closing inventory total.
examples.zh: 我们计算期末存货总额前，练习先展示了产品成本如何进行「间接费用吸收分配」。

examples.en: Our lecturer explained why overhead absorption could differ from the actual overhead incurred in the month.
examples.zh: 讲师解释了为什么「间接费用吸收分配」的金额可能与当月实际间接费用不同。

collocations: effect of overhead absorption on unit costs

words.enDefinition: the measure, such as machine time or labour hours, used to distribute overhead

examples.en: We chose machine hours as the overhead allocation base for costs in the printing department.
examples.zh: 我们用机器工时作为印刷部门成本的「间接费用分配基础」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether the overhead allocation base reflected how the two products used the workshop.
examples.zh: 讲师问，「间接费用分配基础」能不能反映两种产品对工作室的实际使用情况。

words.enDefinition: An amount spent in excess of the budget or other agreed spending limit.

examples.en: The print room recorded an overspend on paper after an unusually busy week of student orders.
examples.zh: 学生订单异常繁忙的一周过后，印刷室记录了一笔纸张费用「超支额」。

examples.en: The worksheet showed an overspend in the repair budget and traced it to two replacement parts.
examples.zh: 练习表显示维修预算有一笔「超支额」，并追溯到两个更换的零件。

words.enDefinition: Removal of a qualifying part of a recognised asset or liability while the remaining part stays recorded.

examples.en: In the case, partial derecognition removed the repaid portion of the debt while the balance remained payable.
examples.zh: 例题中，债务已偿还的部分作「部分终止确认」，余额仍然应付。

examples.en: The tutor used partial derecognition to explain why the retained portion was still on the balance sheet.
examples.zh: 老师用「部分终止确认」说明为什么保留的部分仍在资产负债表上。

collocations: calculate a gain on partial derecognition

words.enDefinition: An approach that involves staff or managers in setting targets they may be responsible for meeting.

examples.en: The case described participative budgeting in which workshop supervisors helped set their own material targets.
examples.zh: 案例介绍了「参与式预算编制」，工场主管会参与设定自己负责的材料目标。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether participative budgeting might improve the accuracy of the printing unit's estimates.
examples.zh: 老师问，「参与式预算编制」是否可能提高印刷部门估算的准确性。

collocations: discuss the benefits of participative budgeting

words.enDefinition: the share of receivables outstanding for which the contractual payment date has already passed

examples.en: The past-due receivables ratio rose while total customer balances stayed almost unchanged during the second quarter.
examples.zh: 第二季度，顾客欠款总额几乎没有变化，但「逾期应收账款占比」上升了。

examples.en: We calculated the past-due receivables ratio using the balances in the agency's monthly ageing schedule.
examples.zh: 我们根据该机构月度账龄表中的余额计算了「逾期应收账款占比」。

words.enDefinition: the interval from the earliest to the latest dates or time limits at which specified payments are due

examples.en: The note compared the payment due date range under the arrangement with that for similar ordinary trade payables.
examples.zh: 附注比较了安排内和类似普通应付账款的「付款到期日范围」。

examples.en: Readers asked for the payment due date range to see when those invoices would have to be settled.
examples.zh: 读者要求查看「付款到期日范围」，以了解这些发票何时必须结清。

collocations: disclose a payment due date range
explain the payment due date range
compare the payment due date range

words.enDefinition: the middle value of a measure for a comparison group

examples.en: The worksheet compared the retailer's operating margin with the peer median for the same period.
examples.zh: 练习表把零售商的营业利润率与同期「同行中位数」作了比较。

examples.en: We recalculated the peer median after removing a company with an unrelated business model.
examples.zh: 剔除一家商业模式不同的公司后，我们重新计算了「同行中位数」。

collocations: a figure below the peer median

words.enDefinition: the change relative to the starting amount, expressed as a percentage

examples.en: The percentage change was larger for the smaller store despite a similar rise measured in pounds.
examples.zh: 两家店按英镑计的增幅相近，但小店的「百分比变动」更大。

examples.en: The class calculated percentage change after checking which value belonged in the starting column.
examples.zh: 同学们先核对基准栏里该用哪个数，再算「百分比变动」。

words.enDefinition: the difference between two values already expressed as percentages

examples.en: The exercise reported a percentage-point change when the margin rose from eight to ten percent.
examples.zh: 利润率从百分之八升至百分之十时，练习报告了「百分点变动」。

examples.en: Our chart showed the percentage-point change in each expense category's share of total revenue.
examples.zh: 图表显示各费用类别占总收入比例的「百分点变动」。

words.enDefinition: A comparison of reported results with the figures planned in the budget.

examples.en: The workbook tracked performance against budget for both product sales and the workshop's monthly supply costs.
examples.zh: 练习册跟踪产品销售和工场月度物料成本的「预算执行表现」。

examples.en: Our group assessed performance against budget before discussing whether the original attendance estimate had been realistic.
examples.zh: 我们组先评估「预算执行表现」，再讨论最初的人数估计是否现实。

collocations: a report on performance against budget

words.enDefinition: A misleading performance figure caused by the way results are measured

examples.en: The old asset values caused a performance measurement distortion in the comparative report.
examples.zh: 旧资产价值造成对照报告中的「绩效衡量失真」。

examples.en: We discussed how shared cost allocations created performance measurement distortion in the sample figures.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了共同成本分摊如何让样本数据产生「绩效衡量失真」。

collocations: an example of performance measurement distortion

words.enDefinition: Under IFRS 15, a promise to transfer a distinct good or service, bundle, or qualifying series to a customer.

examples.en: The sample contract contained a performance obligation to provide twelve months of access to the online service.
examples.zh: 示例合同中有一项「履约义务」，是提供十二个月的在线服务使用权限。

examples.en: Our tutor asked when the company satisfied the performance obligation for the equipment it had promised to deliver.
examples.zh: 老师问，公司什么时候履行了交付承诺设备的「履约义务」。

collocations: allocate the transaction price to a performance obligation

words.enDefinition: A difference that continues across reporting periods and may indicate an underlying change or issue.

examples.en: The report showed a persistent variance after three months of higher charges for the same quantity of paper.
examples.zh: 相同数量的纸连续三个月收费偏高，报告因此显示出「持续性差异」。

examples.en: A persistent variance in support hours prompted the class to recheck the assumptions in its exercise.
examples.zh: 支持服务工时出现「持续性差异」，这让同学们重新核对练习里的假设。

collocations: a persistent variance across several months

words.enDefinition: a schedule reconciling the actual units available with units completed, lost or still in process

examples.en: The physical flow schedule showed how many units remained unfinished at the end of the month.
examples.zh: 「实物数量流程表」显示月底还有多少件没做完。

examples.en: We completed the physical flow schedule before calculating equivalent units for direct materials and conversion.
examples.zh: 我们填完「实物数量流程表」后，才计算直接材料和加工的约当产量。

words.enDefinition: allocating joint costs according to physical quantities such as weight, volume or units at split-off

examples.en: The physical-measure method allocated common costs using the weight of each material after the first process.
examples.zh: 「实物量分配法」用首道工序后每种材料的重量来分配共同成本。

examples.en: We tried the physical-measure method even though the outputs differed greatly in their selling prices.
examples.zh: 尽管各项产出的售价相差很大，我们还是试用了「实物量分配法」。

collocations: compare results under the physical-measure method

words.enDefinition: The number of units to be made during a period according to the production plan or budget.

examples.en: We calculated planned production units before estimating how much paper the print shop would need.
examples.zh: 我们先算出「计划生产数量」，再估算印刷店需要多少纸。

examples.en: The case increased planned production units because the workshop wanted more finished stock by June.
examples.zh: 案例提高了「计划生产数量」，因为工场想在六月前备好更多成品库存。

collocations: use planned production units in the materials budget

words.enDefinition: The part of a variance caused by comparing an original budget or standard with a revision based on changed assumptions.

examples.en: The planning variance captured the impact of the new material price on the original budget assumptions.
examples.zh: 「计划差异」反映材料新价格对原预算假设的影响。

examples.en: With the revised demand estimate, we could calculate the planning variance before looking at actual results.
examples.zh: 有了修订后的需求估算，我们可以先计算「计划差异」，再看实际结果。

collocations: separate the planning variance from operations
explain the cause of a planning variance

words.zhGloss: 全厂统一间接费用分配率
words.enDefinition: one overhead rate used across an entire manufacturing facility
acceptedZhAnswers: 全厂统一间接费用分配率

examples.en: The case used a plantwide overhead rate before comparing results from separate rates for two departments.
examples.zh: 案例先用「全厂统一间接费用分配率」，再比较两个部门各自采用费率算出的结果。

examples.en: We calculated the plantwide overhead rate from total estimated overhead and machine hours for the facility.
examples.zh: 我们根据工厂预估的总间接费用及机器工时计算了「全厂统一间接费用分配率」。

words.enDefinition: cash committed as security for a loan or another obligation

examples.en: The lender could claim pledged cash if the borrower failed to meet the terms of the agreement.
examples.zh: 如果借款人没有履行协议条款，贷款机构可以对「用作担保的现金」主张权利。

examples.en: We reviewed the note that identified pledged cash and explained when the lender would release the funds.
examples.zh: 我们看了说明哪部分属于「用作担保的现金」以及贷款机构何时解押的附注。

words.enDefinition: Recognising revenue when the customer obtains control and the performance obligation is satisfied at a single point.

examples.en: The exercise applied point-in-time revenue recognition when the customer took control of the equipment at delivery.
examples.zh: 顾客在交付时取得设备控制权，例题选择「在某一时点确认收入」。

examples.en: Our tutor compared point-in-time revenue recognition for the equipment with the pattern for the ongoing support service.
examples.zh: 老师对比了设备「在某一时点确认收入」的做法和持续支持服务的确认方式。

collocations: an example of point-in-time revenue recognition
explain point-in-time revenue recognition at delivery

words.enDefinition: an entity's stated accounting policy for determining which investments or cash management balances qualify as cash equivalents

examples.en: The policy for determining cash equivalents explained how the company assessed the remaining term of acquired investments.
examples.zh: 「现金等价物认定政策」说明了公司怎样评估购入投资的剩余期限。

examples.en: We read the policy for determining cash equivalents before checking which holdings appeared in the statement's closing total.
examples.zh: 核对报表期末合计包括哪些投资前，我们读了「现金等价物认定政策」。

collocations: disclose a policy for determining cash equivalents
review the policy for determining cash equivalents
change the policy for determining cash equivalents

words.enDefinition: An obligation from a past event whose existence depends on one or more uncertain future events.

examples.en: The pending decision left a possible obligation because the company disputed whether it was responsible for the damage.
examples.zh: 由于公司对责任认定持异议，未作出的裁决意味着仍存在「潜在义务」。

examples.en: Our group discussed whether the possible obligation would become clearer when the independent review was complete.
examples.zh: 我们组讨论了，独立调查结束后，这项「潜在义务」会不会更明朗。

collocations: evaluate whether a possible obligation exists
disclose the nature of a possible obligation

words.enDefinition: available capacity after allowing for normal breaks, maintenance and other unavoidable interruptions

examples.en: Our practical capacity estimate allowed for staff breaks and scheduled maintenance on the equipment.
examples.zh: 我们估算「实际可供使用的产能」时考虑了员工休息和设备的计划内维护。

examples.en: The exercise calculated an hourly cost from practical capacity rather than assuming uninterrupted operation.
examples.zh: 练习依据「实际可供使用的产能」计算每小时成本，不假定可以一直运转。

collocations: cost per hour of practical capacity

words.enDefinition: A demanding standard that allows for normal losses and interruptions under efficient operating conditions.

examples.en: The students set a practical standard that allowed time to clean the mixer between batches of dough.
examples.zh: 学生设定了「可实现标准」，给每批面团之间的搅拌机清洁留出时间。

examples.en: A practical standard still challenged our team, even though it allowed a small amount of unavoidable waste.
examples.zh: 虽然允许少量不可避免的浪费，「可实现标准」对我们组仍有挑战性。

collocations: allow for downtime in a practical standard

words.enDefinition: an overhead allocation rate calculated in advance from budgeted overhead and expected activity

examples.en: The predetermined overhead rate was set before the workshop knew its actual spending for the year.
examples.zh: 工作室还不知道全年实际花费时，就定下了「预定间接费用分配率」。

examples.en: We used the predetermined overhead rate for all jobs completed during the example month.
examples.zh: 我们对示例月份内所有完工的作业都用了「预定间接费用分配率」。
